2. the front or the uppermost part of a ship , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
3. the shoulder-strap of a tunic, (Euripides) (ML)

G7492.definition: a lover , properly of persons, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.:—;metaphorically of things, τυραννίδος (Herdotus Historicus); πολέμων (Euripides); ἐρ. πραγμάτων = πολυπράγμων, (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐρ. τοῦ πονεῖν fond of work, (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐρ. ἐπαίνου (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7501.definition: a prop, stay, support , Lat. columen, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;in plural the props to keep a boat on shore upright, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G7505.definition:
a day-labourer, hired servant of any sort; in (Iliad by Homer), ἔριθοι are mowers or reapers : later, ἔριθοι, αἱ, spinsters, workers in wool , (Demosthenes Orator) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G7508.definition: 1. to creep, crawl , Lat. serpo, repo, and generally to move slowly, walk , (Homer); of reports, to creep on, spread , like Lat. serpit rumor, (Sophocles Tragicus); ὁ πόλεμος ἑρπέτω let it take its course , (Aristophanes Comicus); of calamities, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7509.definition: a redness on the skin , (Thucydides); ἐρ. προσώπου a blush , (Euripides):—;absolute redness , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7512.definition: the heron or hern , Lat. ardea, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G7513.definition:
1. love , [variant datesTragica Adespota:—; love of a thing, desire for it, τινός (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;in plural loves, amours , (Euripides); in (Sophocles Tragicus), of passionate joy , compare φρίσσω II. 3. 
2. as proper noun the god of love, Eros, Amor , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7514.definition:
ἑσπερινός, -ή, -όν
(= the more frequently ἑσπέριος, -α, -ον), [in LXX for עֶרֶב, 4Ki.16:15, Psa.141:2, al. ;] 
of the evening, evening: Luk.12:38 (WH, - mg. -).†
(AS)

G7516.definition:
1. the hearth, fire-place , (Homer); the sanctuary of suppliants, καθέζετο ἐπ᾽ ἐσχάρῃ ἐν κονίῃσιν (Odyssey by Homer):—; a pan of coals, a brasier , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. πυρὸς ἐσχάραι the watch-fires of the camp, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. an altar for burnt-offerings , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G7522.definition:
1. a companion , (Iliad by Homer); φόρμιγξ, ἣν δαιτὶ θεοὶ ποίησαν ἑταίρην (Odyssey by Homer); πενία σφιν ἑταίρα (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
2. opposite to a lawful wife, a concubine, a courtesan , (Herdotus Historicus), attic (ML)

G7526.definition: coupled with an animal of diverse kind , (Septuagint Greek Bible) (ML)

G7528.definition: easy to be taken or caught , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

G7529.definition:
1. well-joined, harmonious , (Euripides) 
2. of men, accommodating , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7530.definition:
1. adverb well, rightly , to confirm or approve what has been said, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;ironically, (Euripides) 
2. without a Verb, good! well said! well done! bravo! Lat. euge! (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7531.definition: nobility of birth, high descent , (Aeschulus Tragicus); εὐγένεια παίδων = εὐγενεῖς παῖδες, (Euripides) (ML)

G7532.definition:
1. well-known, familiar , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. easy to discern , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G7533.definition: to be of good repute, to be held in esteem, honoured, famous, popular , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.: —; εὐδ. ἔν τινι to be distinguished in a thing, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐπί τινι (Plato Philosophus):—; εὐδ. παρὰ τῷ βασιλέϊ to have influence with him, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7535.definition: of good hope, hopeful, cheerful, sanguine , (Thucydides), etc.:—;with infinitive future, εὔελπις ἰσχύσειν (Aeschulus Tragicus); εὔελπις σωθήσεσθαι in good hope to be saved, (Thucydides) (ML)

G7536.definition:
1. well-girdled , of women, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. of men, girt up for exercise, dressed for walking, active , (Horace)'s alte praecinctus , (Herdotus Historicus); of light troops, unincumbered , Lat. expeditus, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. metaphorically unincumbered , πενία (Plutarch) (ML)

G7541.definition:
1. to thrive, flourish, prosper , Lat. florere, vigere, (Herdotus Historicus):—;with dative to abound in a thing, (Homeric Hymns) 
2. Pass. in same sense, οἱ Λακεδαιμόνιοι εὐθηνήθησαν (Herdotus Historicus); τὴν πόλιν εὐθενεῖσθαι (Demosthenes Orator) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G7546.definition: easy to be despised, contemptible, despicable , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7547.definition: of good report, famous, glorious , (Homer), etc.; εὐκλεέστατος βίος (Euripides) adverb -εῶς, epic -ειῶς, (Iliad by Homer); κατθανεῖν (Aeschulus Tragicus); Sup. εὐκλεέστατα, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7549.definition:
1. of persons, easily satisfied, contented with one's food , [variant datesAnthology Palantina, (Plutarch) 
2. easily satisfied, contented, good-natured, peaceable , Lat. facilis, comis, (Aristophanes Comicus); with dative, εὔκολος πολίταις friendly to them, at peace with them, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;adverb -λως, tranquilly, calmly , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. willing, agile , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
4. in bad sense, easily led, prone , πρὸς ἀδικίαν (Lucian) 
5. of things, easy , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7550.definition:
1. sweetly-speaking , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. = εὔγλωσσος II, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G7551.definition: of good size, very large , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7553.definition: of a good length, tall , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7554.definition: easy to pass , of mountains, (Xenophon Historicus); of a road, easy to travel , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7556.definition:
to be well off, enjoy oneself, make merry , (Herdotus Historicus) 
from εὐπᾶθής (ML)

G7557.definition:
1. with fine purple border , (Plutarch) 
2. of persons, wearing such a garment , Lat. praetextatus, a grandee, (Lucian) (ML)

G7558.definition:
1. well-looking, goodly, comely , of outward appearance, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; εὐπρ. ἰδεῖν fair to look on, (Xenophon Historicus); εἶδος εὐπρεπής (Euripides) 
2. decent, seemly, fitting, becoming , (Herdotus Historicus); τελευτὴ εὐπρεπεστάτη a most glorious end, (Thucydides) 
3. specious, plausible , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐκ τοῦ εὐπρεποῦς in pretence , (Thucydides) 
4. adverb -πῶς, ionic πέως, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; comparative -πέστερον, (Euripides); Sup. -πέστατα, (Thucydides) (ML)

G7559.definition:
1. fair of face , (Aristophanes Comicus): with glad countenance , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. metaphorically fair in outward show, specious , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G7561.definition:
1. an invention, discovery , (Euripides), etc. 
2. with genitive an invention, for or against a thing, a remedy , (Euripides) 
3. that which is found unexpectedly , i. e., much like Ἕρμαιον, a piece of good luck, godsend, windfall, prize , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
4. of a child, a foundling , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7563.definition: breadth, width , absolute, εὖρος in breadth , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; so, τὸ εὖρος (Xenophon Historicus); εἰς εὖρος (Euripides) (ML)

G7564.definition:
1. wide, broad , (Homer), etc. 
2. far-reaching, far-spread , κλέος εὐρύ (Odyssey by Homer); ἐλπίδες [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
3. as adverb the neuter εὐρύ is mostly used, (Iliad by Homer), etc. (ML)

G7565.definition: to be or become mouldy , βίος εὐρωτιῶν the life of the unwashed , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7567.definition:
to be steady, favourable , (Euripides):—; to be calm, tranquil , of the sea, (Lucian) 
from εὐστᾶθής (ML)

G7572.definition:
1. easily handled, easy to deal with, easy , εὐχερές ἐστι, with infinitive, (Batrachomyomachia); πάντα ταῦτ᾽ ἐν εὐχερεῖ ἔθου didst make light of them, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;adverb -ρῶς, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. of persons, manageable, accommodating, kind, yielding , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;adverb, εὐχερῶς φέρειν (Plato Philosophus), etc.; comparative -έστερον, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. in bad sense, unscrupulous, reckless , (Demosthenes Orator):—;adverb -ρῶς, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G7579.definition:
1. to bind on or to , λύουσα ἢ ' φάπτουσα undoing or making fast , (Sophocles Tragicus); τοὖργον ὡς ἐφάψειεν τόδε that she had made fast (i. e. perpetrated) the deed, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., 3rd singular perfect and pluperfect ἐφῆπται, -το, is or was hung over one, impends over, is fixed as one's doom , with dative, Τρώεσσι κήδεe ἐφῆπται (Iliad by Homer) 
2. Mid. to lay hold of, grasp, reach , with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 
3. to lay hold of with the mind, attain to , Lat. assequi, with genitive, (Plato Philosophus) 
4. in (Pindar) also with dative (like θιγγάνω, ψαύω); to apply oneself to. 
5. (Herdotus Historicus) uses participle perfect passive with genitive, εἴδεος ἐπαμμένος possessed of a certain degree of beauty. 
6. to follow, come next , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G7580.definition:
1. to draw on, drag or trail after one, ἐπ. τὰς οὐράς, of long-tailed sheep, (Herdotus Historicus); ἵππον ἐκ τοῦ βραχίονος ἐπ. to lead a horse by a rein upon the arm, (Herdotus Historicus); ναῦς ὡς ἐφέλξω will take in tow , (Euripides) 
2. to bring on, bring in its train , (Euripides) 
3. to drink off , (Euripides) 
4. Pass., ἐφελκομένοισι πόδεσσι with feet trailing after him, of one who is dragged lifeless away, (Iliad by Homer); ἐφέλκετο ἔγχος, i. e. sticking in his hand, (Iliad by Homer); ἐπελκόμενος trailing behind , of a boat, (Herdotus Historicus); οἱ ἐπελκόμενοι the stragglers of an army, (Herdotus Historicus) 
5. to be attracted , (Homeric Hymns) 
6. Mid. to draw to oneself, attract , αὐτὸς γὰρ ἐφέλκεται ἄνδρα σίδηρος the very sight of arms attracts men, i. e. tempts them to use it , (Odyssey by Homer) 
7. to draw or pull over , (Plutarch); ἐφ. ὀφρῦς to frown, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
8. to bring on consequences, (Euripides) 
9. to assume , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7582.definition:
1. boiled, dressed , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. ἑφθὸς χρυσός refined gold, (Simonides Lyricus) (ML)

G7583.definition:
1. to visit, go the rounds, patrol , (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass., ἐφοδεύεται the rounds are made , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. with dative to watch over , ἀγῶσιν (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G7584.definition:
1. to furnish with supplies for a journey , Lat. viaticum dare, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. Mid., πενταδραχμίαν ἑκάστῳ ἐφοδιασάμενος having seen that five drachms were paid to each, (Xenophon Historicus):—;metaphorically to maintain , ἀργίαν (Plutarch) (ML)

G7586.definition:
1. to oversee, observe, survey , of the sun, (Homer):—;then of the gods, to watch over, observe, take notice of , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; of a general going his rounds, (Thucydides); to visit the sick, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. simply, to look upon, view, behold , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;Pass., ὅσον ἐφεωρᾶτο τῆς νήσου as much of it as was in view , (Thucydides) 
3. to look out, choose , ἐπιόψομαι ἥτις ἀρίστη (Odyssey by Homer), etc. (ML)

G7591.definition:
1. the urchin, hedgehog , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
2. the sea-urchin , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. the shell of the sea-urchin , often used as a cup : then like Lat. testa, a pot, jug, pitcher, Lat. echinus, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.:—; the vase in which the notes of evidence were deposited, (Demosthenes Orator) 
4. in plural sharp points at each end of a bit, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7594.definition:
1. to boil, seethe , (Herdotus Historicus), attic: proverbial of useless labour, λίθον ἕψεις (Aristophanes Comicus); with genitive partitive, ἥψομεν τοῦ κορκόρου we boiled some pimpernel, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass. to be boiled , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. of metals, to smelt, refine , (Pindar) 
3. metaphorically, γῆρας ἀνώνυμον ἕψειν to cherish an inglorious age, (Pindar) (ML)

G7595.definition: in the morning, early , (Herdotus Historicus): —; τὸ ἑωθινόν, as adverb, early in the morning , (Herdotus Historicus); so, ἐξ ἑωθινοῦ = ἕωθεν, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7599.definition:
1. to yoke, put to , ἵππους (Homer), etc.; ζ. ἵππους ὑφ᾽ ἅρματα, ὑφ᾽ ἅρμασιν, ὑπ᾽ ὄχεσφιν, ὑπ᾽ ἀμάξηισιν (Iliad by Homer);—;(so in Mid., ἵππους ζεύγνυσθαι to put to one's horses, (Homer));—;also of riding horses, to harness, saddle and bridle , ζεῦξαι Πάγασον (Pindar):—;of chariots, to put to, get ready , (Homer) 
2. to bind, bind fast , (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass., φάρη ἐζευγμέναι having them fastened , (Euripides) 
3. metaphorically, πότμωι ζυγείς in the yoke of fate, (Pindar); ἀνάγκηι, ὁρκίοις ζυγείς (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. to join together , σανίδες ἐζευγμέναι well-joined , (Iliad by Homer) 
5. to join in wedlock , (Euripides):—;in Mid., of the husband, to wed , (Euripides):—;Pass. to be married , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6. to join opposite banks by bridges , τὸν Ἑλλήσποντον ζεῦξαι (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;also, γέφυραν ζεῦξαι to form a bridge, (Herdotus Historicus) 
7. to undergird ships with ropes , (Thucydides) (ML)

G7602.definition:
1. to be emulated, worthy of imitation , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. to be deemed happy, to be envied , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc. 
3. of conditions, enviable, blessed , (Euripides) (ML)

G7605.definition: to yoke together , ζ. κιθάραν to put the cross-bar to the lyre, (Lucian) (ML)

G7609.definition: to paint from life, to paint , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7611.definition: Lat. jus, sauce to eat with meat, fish, etc., (Aristophanes Comicus); ὁ μέλας ζ. the black broth of Spartans, (Plutarch) (ML)

G7614.definition: to kindle into flame, light up : metaphorically, ζ. τάρβος (Aeschulus Tragicus); νείκη (Euripides) (ML)

G7616.definition:
1. ready to lead or guide , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. fit to command, authoritative, leading , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
3. = Rom. Consularis , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7618.definition:
1. one must lead , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. one must suppose , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7619.definition: to sweeten, season, give a flavour or relish to a thing, with accusative, (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

G7620.definition:
1. sweet to the taste or smell, (Homer); to the hearing, (Homer); then of any pleasant feeling or state, as sleep, (Homer):—;with infinitive, ἡδὺς δρακεῖν (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἡδὺς ἀκοῦσαι λόγος (Plato Philosophus):—; ἡδύ ἐστι or γίγνεται it is pleasant , (Homer), etc.:—;so, οὔ μοι ἥδιόν ἐστι λέγειν I had rather not say, (Herdotus Historicus):—;neuter as Substantive, τὰ ἡδέα pleasures , (Thucydides):—;neuter as adverb, sweetly , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. after (Homer), of persons, pleasant, welcome , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. well-pleased, glad , (Sophocles Tragicus); in addressing a person, ὦ ἥδιστε, Horace's dulcissime rerum , (Plato Philosophus) 
4. like εὐήθης, innocent, simple , ὡς ἡδὺς εἶ (Plato Philosophus) 
5. adverb ἡδέως, sweetly, pleasantly, with pleasure , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; ἡδέως ἂν ἐροίμην I would gladly ask, should like to ask, (Demosthenes Orator);—; ἡδ. ἔχειν τι to be pleased or content with, (Euripides); ἡδ. ἔχειν πρός τινα or τινί to be kind, well-disposed to one, (Demosthenes Orator):—; comparative ἥδιον (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;Sup., ἥδιστα (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7621.definition: that which gives a relish or flavour, seasoning, sauce , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

G7626.definition:
electron , a word sometimes used to denote amber , as probably in (Homer) and (Herdotus Historicus);—;sometimes pale gold , a compound of 1 part of silver to 4 of gold, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.—;In (Aristophanes Comicus) ἐκπιπτουσῶν τῶν ἠλέκτρων, the ἤλεκτροι are probably the pegs of the lyre made of or inlaid with electron. 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G7627.definition: Dep.:—; to sit in the court Ἡλιαία, be a Heliast , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7629.definition:
1. a half-ass , i. e. a mule , (Homer), etc.:—; proverbial, ἐπεὰν ἡμίονοι τέκωσι, i. e. never, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. the ἡμ. ἀγροτέρα of (Iliad by Homer) 2. 851 is probably the wild ass. 
3. as adjective, βρέφος ἡμίονον a mule- foal, (Iliad by Homer); ἡμ. βασιλεύς a mule- king, half-Mede half-Persian, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7633.definition:
1. one who holds the reins, a driver, charioteer , opposite to παραιβάτης (the warrior by his side), (Iliad by Homer) 
2. generally a chariot-driver , as in the games, (Pindar), attic:—;in (Theognis Elegiacus), a rider. 
3. metaphorically a guide, governor , (Pindar) (ML)

G7634.definition: the liver , (Homer), etc.:—; ὑφ᾽ ἥπατος φέρειν, of pregnant women, (Euripides):—;in [variant datesTragica Adespota as the seat of the passions, anger, fear, etc., answering therefore to our "heart." (ML)

G7636.definition:
1. a hero, in (Homer) used of the Greeks before Troy, then of warriors generally; and then of all free men of the heroic age, as the minstrel Demodocus, the herald Mulius, even the unwarlike Phaeacians. 
2. in (Hesiod) the blessed heroes are the fourth age of men, who fell before Thebes and Troy, and then passed to the Islands of the Blest. 
3. heroes, as objects of worship, demigods or men born from a god and a mortal, as Hercules, Aeneas, Memnon, (Herdotus Historicus); then of such as had done great services to mankind, as Daedalus, Triptolemus, Theseus, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
4. later, the heroes are inferior local deities , patrons of tribes, cities, guilds, founders of cities, etc.; as at Athens, the ἥρωες ἐπώνυμοι were the heroes after whom the φυλαί were named , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7637.definition: stilly, quietly, softly, gently , (Pindar); ἔχ᾽ ἡσυχῆ keep quiet , (Plato Philosophus); ἡς. γελάσαι (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7638.definition:
1. a sound , but properly of a returned sound, echo , (Homeric Hymns), etc. 
2. generally, a ringing sound , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7639.definition:
1. to bloom, abound, to be luxuriant , of fruit-trees, (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; often in participle perfect τεθηλώς, epic feminine τεθαλυῖα, as adjective, luxuriant, exuberant , (Odyssey by Homer); with accusative cognate, οὐ δένδρε᾽ ἔθαλλεν χῶρος the place grew no trees, θαλλούσης βίον ἐλαίας (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. of other natural objects, τεθαλυῖα ἐέρση the fresh or copious dew, (Odyssey by Homer); τεθαλυῖα ἀλοιφῆι rich with fat, (Iliad by Homer); εἰλαπίνηι τεθαλυίηι at a sumptuous feast, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. of men, to bloom, flourish , (Hesiod), etc. 
4. in bad sense, to be active , νόσος ἀεὶ τέθηλε (Sophocles Tragicus); πήματα ἀεὶ θάλλοντα (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7654.definition: feminine of θεράπων, a waiting maid, handmaid , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G7656.definition: a hunter, huntsman , (Iliad by Homer); κυσὶ θηρευτῇσι (Iliad by Homer); also of a fisher , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7661.definition:
1. hot, warm , θερμὰ λοετρά (Homer); of tears, (Homer), etc. 
2. metaphorically hot, hasty, rash, headlong , like Lat. calidus, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
3. still warm, fresh , ἴχνη [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
4. τὸ θερμόν = θερμότης, heat , Lat. calor, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
5. θερμόν (i.e. ὕδωρ); hot water , θερμῷ λοῦσθαι (Aristophanes Comicus) 
6. τὰ θερμά (entry χωρία); (Herdotus Historicus): but (entry λουτρά); hot baths , (Xenophon Historicus) 
7. adverb -μῶς, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7662.definition:
1. a setting, placing, arranging , (Pindar); θ. νόμων lawgiving , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. a deposit of money, preparatory to a law-suit, (Aristophanes Comicus): money paid in advance, earnest-money , (Demosthenes Orator) 
3. position, situation , Lat. situs, of a city, (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

G7663.definition:
1. like θέμις, that which is laid down and established, a law, ordinance , Lat. institutum, λέκτροιο θεσμὸν ἵκοντο, i. e. they fulfilled the established law of wedlock, (Odyssey by Homer); so in (Herdotus Historicus) and attic 
2. at Athens, Draco's laws were called θεσμοί, because each began with the word θεσμός (compare θεσμοθέτης); while (Solon Lyricus)'s laws were named νόμοι. 
3. an institution, ordinance , as the court of Areopagus, (Aeschulus Tragicus); of the great games, (Pindar) (ML)

G7668.definition:
1. a wild beast, beast of prey , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; joined with λέων, (Euripides); with λέαινα, [variant datesAnthology Palantina; also of Cerberus, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;in plural beasts , as opposite to birds and fishes, (Odyssey by Homer), etc. 
2. of any animal , as of birds, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
3. any fabulous monster , as the sphinx, (Aeschulus Tragicus); especially a centaur , (Sophocles Tragicus) (compare Φήρ)); a satyr , (Euripides) (ML)

G7672.definition:
a store, treasure , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
from θησαυρίζω (ML)

G7674.definition:
1. a band or company marching through the streets with dance and song , especially in honour of Bacchus, a band of revellers , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. generally, any party, company, troop , (Euripides) (ML)

G7676.definition:
1. a heap , (Odyssey by Homer):—;in plural sand-heaps, sand-bank , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. the beach, shore , παρὰ θῖνα θαλάσσης (Iliad by Homer); παρὰ θῖν᾽ ἁλός (Iliad by Homer); so, ἐπὶ θινί (Odyssey by Homer) 
3. sand or mud at the bottom of the sea, οἶδμα κυλίνδει βυσσόθεν θῖνα (Sophocles Tragicus); metaphorically, τὸν θῖνά μου ταράττεις you trouble the very bottom of my heart, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7682.definition:
1. muddy, foul, thick, troubled , Lat. turbidus, properly of water, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. metaphorically troubled by passion or madness , θολεροὶ λόγοι (Aeschulus Tragicus); θολερῷ χειμῶνι with turbid storm of madness, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7683.definition:
1. courage, boldness , (Iliad by Homer); θρ. ἰσχύος confidence in strength, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. in bad sense, over-boldness, daring, rashness, audacity, impudence , attic, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7685.definition:
1. = θαρσύνω, to make bold, embolden, encourage , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass. and Mid., to be bold or ready, take courage , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
2. Pass., in bad sense, to be over-bold, audacious, to speak boldly or insolently , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7686.definition:
1. bold, spirited, courageous, confident , (Homer), attic; θρασεῖα τοῦ μέλλοντος full of confidence for the future, (Thucydides) 
2. in bad sense, over-bold, rash, venturous , Lat. audax, (Odyssey by Homer), attic 
3. of things, to be ventured , with infinitive, θρασύ μοι τόδ᾽ εἰπεῖν this I am bold to say, (Pindar); οὐκ ἆρ᾽ ἐκείνῳ προσμῖξαι θρασ; (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. adverb -έως: comparative θρασύτερον, too boldly , (Thucydides) (ML)

G7688.definition:
that which is broken, a fragment, wreck, piece , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
from * θραύω (ML)

G7694.definition: an African tree with scented wood , a kind of juniper or cedar , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G7696.definition:
1. a bag, pouch, wallet , (Herdotus Historicus); δερῶ σε θύλακον I'll make a bag of your skin, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. in plural the trousers of the Persians, (Euripides) (ML)

G7697.definition:
1. that which is slain or offered, a victim, sacrifice, offering , [variant datesTragica Adespota, (Thucydides), etc.; πάγκαρπα θ. offerings of all fruits, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. sacrifice , as an act, (Sophocles Tragicus): metaphorically, θ. λεύσιμον a sacrifice to be avenged by stoning [the murderers, 6th/5th c.BC] (ML)

G7705.definition: medical treatment : metaphorically a curing, correcting , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G7707.definition:
1. to treat medically, to cure , (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass. to be under medical care , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. absolute to practise medicine , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G7708.definition: the ibis , an Egyptian bird, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7709.definition: the part behind the thigh and knee, the ham , Lat. poples, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G7711.definition:
1. to make to sit down, to seat , (Homer), etc.; αὐτός τε κάθησο καὶ ἄλλους ἵδρυε λαούς (Iliad by Homer); ἵδρυσε τὴν στρατιήν encamped the army, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to be seated, sit. still , (Iliad by Homer); of an army, to lie encamped , (Herdotus Historicus); ἀσφαλῶς ἱδρυμένος seated, steady, secure , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. like Lat. figere, to fix or settle persons in a place, εἰς δόμον (Euripides):—;Pass. to be settled , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
3. in Mid. to establish , ἱδρ. τινὰ ἄνακτα (Euripides); τινὰ ἐς οἶκόν (Euripides) 
4. perfect passive ἵδρυ_μαι, of places, to be situated, to lie , (Herdotus Historicus) 
5. to set up, found , especially to dedicate temples, statues, (Euripides):—;Pass., ἱρόν, βωμὸς ἵδρυται (Herdotus Historicus):—;Mid. to set up for oneself, to found , (Herdotus Historicus); perfect passive in middle sense, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7714.definition:
1. to approach as a suppliant , ἐπεί σε ἱκέτευσα (Odyssey by Homer); ἐς Πηλῆ= ἱκέτευσε (Iliad by Homer); ἱκ. τινὰ γονάτων or πρὸς γονάτων (Euripides) 
2. to supplicate, beseech one to do a thing, with accusative et infinitive, (Odyssey by Homer), attic:—;also with genitive pers. et infinitive to beg of one that . ., (Euripides) 
3. with accusative rei, to ask a thing as a suppliant , (Euripides) (ML)

G7715.definition: one who comes to seek protection, a suppliant or fugitive , who lays his ἱκετηρία on the altar or hearth, after which his person was inviolable; especially one who seeks purification after homicide , (Homer), etc. (ML)

G7720.definition:
mud, slime, dirt , (Iliad by Homer) 
Gen. ἰλυ_ος (Homer), ἰλῦος [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G7722.definition: an appearance , Lat. species, [variant datesAnthology Palantina, (Lucian) (ML)

G7723.definition:
1. a fowler, bird-catcher , [Refs 2nd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. as adjective catching with birdlime , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G7725.definition:
1. to drive horses, drive a chariot , (Iliad by Homer): later, to ride , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. Pass., of the horse, to be ridden or driven , (Plato Philosophus): to be broken in for riding , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. ἱππάζεσθαι χώραν to ride over a country, (Plutarch) (ML)

G7728.definition:
1. to be a horseman or rider, to ride , (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;so in Mid., (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. metaphorically of the wind, (Euripides) 
3. to be a trooper, serve in the cavalry , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. of a horse, as we say "the horse rides (i. e. carries his rider ) well," (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7729.definition:
1. a chariot-road , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. a race-course for chariots, Lat. curriculum, (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)

G7730.definition: to make equal , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—;Mid., ὄνυχας χεῖράς τε ἰσώσαντο, i. e. used them in like manner, (Hesiod):—;Pass. to be made like or equal to , with dative, (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G7732.definition: any web, a sail , ἱστία στέλλεσθαι, μηρύεσθαι, καθελεῖν to lower or furl sail , (Odyssey by Homer); ἄκροισι χρῆσθαι ἱστίοις to keep the sails close-reefed, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7733.definition:
1. anything set upright : 
2. a ship's mast , ἱστὸν στῆσαι or στήσασθαι to step the mast , (Homer):—; a rod, pole , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. the beam of the loom, which stood upright , instead of lying horizontal as in our looms, (Homer); ἱστὸν στήσασθαι to set up the beam and so begin a web, (Hesiod); ἱστὸν ἐποίχεσθαι to traverse the loom , because the weaver was obliged to walk to and fro, (Homer) 
4. the warp that was fixed to the beam, the web , (Homer) (ML)

G7734.definition:
1. the hip-joint , (Homer) 
2. in plural the fleshy parts round the hip-joint, the haunches, hams , (Iliad by Homer) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G7735.definition:
checked in one's voice, stuttering, stammering , (Herdotus Historicus) 
(ML)

G7739.definition: headlong, hasty, eager, ready for anything, reckless, Lat. audax, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G7740.definition:
1. a willow , Lat. salix, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. a wicker shield, target , (Euripides) (ML)

G7741.definition: fishy, scaly , i. e. foul, dirty , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7743.definition:
1. to track out, hunt after, seek out , (Sophocles Tragicus): metaphorically, τὴν ψῆφον ἰχν. seeking for the vote of condemnation, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. ἰχν. ὄρη to hunt the mountains, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7744.definition: ichor, the etherial juice , that flows in the veins of gods, (Iliad by Homer);—;epic accusative ἰχῶ for ἰχῶρα, (Iliad by Homer): later blood , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G7745.definition:
Ἰωβήλ, see: Ἰωβήδ.
Ἰωβήδ (WH, -βήλ, Lk, l.with; Rec., RV, Ὠβήδ), ὁ, indecl., 
Jo bed (Obed): Mat.1:5, Luk.3:32.†
(AS)

G7750.definition:
1. a jar or vessel for water or wine , Lat. cadus, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. a liquid measure, = ἀμφορεύς, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
3. an urn or box for collecting the votes , like καδίσκος, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7752.definition: to be clean or pure , (Plato Philosophus): —;with genitive to be clean or free from guilt, (Plutarch); also, κ. ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ (i.e. τοῦ σώματος); (Plato Philosophus); also, καθ. γνώμῃ to be pure or clear in mind, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7754.definition: a cleansing from guilt or defilement, purification , Lat. lustratio, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7758.definition: to sit down , θῶκόνδε καθίζανον they went to the council and took their seats , (Odyssey by Homer); μάντις ἐς θρόνους κ. (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G7761.definition:
1. a going down, descent , (Lucian): a way down , (Lucian) 
2. a coming back, return , (Euripides); of an exile, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7762.definition:
1. to confess or allow , especially to one's detriment, (Plato Philosophus) 
2. to promise, vow , (Lucian) 
3. to betroth , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7764.definition: to treat despitefully, to insult or affront wantontly , τινά (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; also τινός (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., absolute, to wax wanton , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7766.definition: to be fast asleep, fall asleep , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., perfect participle κατυπνωμένος asleep , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7767.definition: to come far behind , (Plutarch): absolute to be behind-hand , Menand. (ML)

G7769.definition: to make new : hence, καί τι καινίζει στέγη and the house has something strange about it, (Sophocles Tragicus); καίνισον ζυγόν try on thy new yoke, handsel it, (Aeschulus Tragicus); κ. εὐχάς to offer new, strange prayers, (Euripides) (ML)

G7770.definition:
1. of Place, in or at the right place , hence of parts of the body, ἐν καιρίῳ, κατὰ καίριον in a vital part , (Iliad by Homer); also, of wounds, πέπληγμαι καιρίαν πληγήν, καιρίας πληγῆς τυχεῖν (Aeschulus Tragicus); πληγή is sometimes omitted, (Herdotus Historicus):—; adverb -ίως, mortally , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. of Time, in season, seasonable, timely, opportune , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. lasting but for a season , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
4. adverb -ρίως, in season, seasonably , (Aeschulus Tragicus): comparative -ωτέρως (Xenophon Historicus):—;so also, πρὸς τὸ καίριον (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7772.definition:
1. the character and conduct of a κακοῦργος, ill-doing, wickedness, villany, malice , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; of a horse, viciousness , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. in plural malpractices , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7774.definition:
1. ill-minded, malicious, malignant , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. imprudent, thoughtless, heedless , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G7776.definition:
1. a vase-shaped basket , Lat. calathus, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. a cooling-vessel, cooler , Virgil (ML)

G7778.definition:
1. made of reed , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. made of cane , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7779.definition: a bit of reed , used as a phial, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7782.definition:
1. beauty , (Homer), etc.:—; ἐς κάλλος with an eye to beauty , so as to set off her beauty, (Euripides); but, εἰς κ. ζῆν for pleasure , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. of persons, a beauty , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. in plural also rich garments and stuffs , (Aeschulus Tragicus); κάλλεα κηροῦ beautiful works of wax, i. e. honeycombs, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G7784.definition:
1. properly, to make the face beautiful; hence, to beautify, embellish , (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass., κεκαλλωπισμέναι τὸ χρῶμα, i. e. painted, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. Mid. to adorn oneself, make oneself fine or smart , (Plato Philosophus): metaphorically to pride oneself in or on a thing, τινι or ἐπί τινι (Plato Philosophus):—;absolute to make a display, shew off , of a horse, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. to be coy, play the prude , τινι or πρός τινα towards another, (Plato Philosophus); with infinitive, κ. παραιτεῖσθαι to affect to deprecate, (Plutarch) (ML)

G7788.definition: Lat. camera, anything with an arched cover, a covered carriage, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7791.definition:
1. a bending, winding , of a river, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. the turning in a race-course, turning-post , (Aristophanes Comicus): metaphorically, μῦθον ἐς καμπὴν ἄγειν to bring a speech to its middle or turning point , (Euripides); καμπὰς ποιεῖσθαι (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7792.definition: bent, crooked, curved , of a bow, (Iliad by Homer); of wheels, (Iliad by Homer); of chariots, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G7793.definition:
1. Lat. cantharus, a beetle worshipped in Egypt, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
2. a Naxian boat , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. a mark or knot like a beetle , on the tongue of the Egyptian god Apis, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7795.definition:
1. a retail-dealer, huckster, hawker, peddlar, higgler , Lat. institor, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; opposite to the merchant ἔμπορος); (Xenophon Historicus), etc.; applied to Darius because of his finance-regulations, (Herdotus Historicus):—; κ. ἀσπίδων, ὅπλων a dealer in . . , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. a tavern-keeper, publican , Lat. caupo, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
3. metaphorically, κ. πονηρίας a dealer in petty roguery, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G7796.definition:
1. to make smoke , i. e. to make a fire , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to smoke, blacken with smoke , (Demosthenes Orator) 
3. intransitive to be black with smoke , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7797.definition:
the caper-plant , or its fruit, the caper , Lat. capparis, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G7802.definition: fruit-bearing, fruitful , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—; κάρπιμα, τά, fruit-trees or corn-fields , (Aristophanes Comicus); κάρπιμα ἀγαθά property that yields a produce , opposite to ἄκαρπα, (Aristotle Philosopher):—;metaphorically, τῶν ξένων τοὺς κ. rich foreigners from whom money can be wrung , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7805.definition:
1. to bear fruit or bear as fruit , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. Mid. to get fruit for oneself , i. e., 
3. to reap crops from land, (Herdotus Historicus): metaphorically to exhaust or drain , τὴν Ἑλλάδα (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. to enjoy the interest of money, (Demosthenes Orator); so in perfect passive, τὸ ἐργαστήριον κεκαρπωμένος enjoying the profits of the shop, (Demosthenes Orator):—;absolute to make profit , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
5. to reap the fruits of, enjoy the free use of , (Thucydides), etc.: —;then, 
6. simply, to enjoy , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—; sometimes in bad sense, καρποῦσθαι τὴν ἁμαρτίαν (Aeschulus Tragicus); πένθη (Euripides) (ML)

G7814.definition: any kind of nut , (Aristophanes Comicus); distinguished into various kinds, as κ. βασιλικά or Περσικά, walnuts , also called simply κάρυα, (Batrachomyomachia); κ. κασταναϊκά or κασταναῖα chestnuts , etc. (ML)

G7818.definition:
tin , Lat. stannum, (Iliad by Homer) It was melted, and then cast upon χαλκός, hence χεῦμα κασσιτέροιο a plating of tin , (Iliad by Homer) 
A foreign word. (ML)

G7821.definition: to bring life to an end , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7823.definition: to cry down, cry out against , with genitive, (Herdotus Historicus); κ. τινῶν ὅτι τὰς σπονδὰς λελυκότες εἶεν (Thucydides); with accusative to bawl down, outcry , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7824.definition: to feed flocks upon or in a place, Lat. depascere, χὠ τὰν Σαμίαν καταβόσκων the shepherd of Samos, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G7829.definition: mockery, derision, ridicule , Lat. ludibrium, ἐμαυτοῦ καταγέλωτα τάδε; these ornaments which bring ridicule upon me? (Aeschulus Tragicus); κ. πλατύς sheer mockery , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὁ κ. τῆς πράξεως the crowning absurdity of the matter, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7830.definition: to grow old , Lat. senescere, (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G7832.definition:
1. to discover and make known , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; with infinitive to give notice that . . , (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass., with participle, κατεδέδεκτο ἐοῦσα χρηστή had been proved to be good, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. to invent and teach, introduce, exhibit , (Aristophanes Comicus); with infinitive to shew how to do, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7834.definition: a tie, band: a magic knot , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G7835.definition:
1. Dep. 
2. to receive, admit , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
3. to receive back, take home again , (Isaeus Orator): —;aor1 passive καταδεχθῆναι in passive sense, (Lucian) (ML)

G7840.definition:
1. intransitive, in active present καταδύνω and middle καταδύομαι:—; to go down, sink, set , of the sun, ἠέλιος κατέδυ (Iliad by Homer); ἐς ἠέλιον καταδύντα till sun set , (Odyssey by Homer); of ships, to be sunk or rather to be disabled (see. infr. II), (Herdotus Historicus):—;of persons, καταδεδυκώς having popped down , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to go down into, plunge into , with accusative, καταδῦναι ὅμιλον, μάχην, δόμον, πόλιν (Homer); followed by a preposition, καταδυσόμεθ᾽ εἰς Ἀί̈δαο δόμους we will go down into . ., (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;with a notion of secresy, to insinuate oneself, steal into , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. to slink away and lie hid , καταδύομαι ὑπὸ τῆς αἰσχύνης (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. to get into, put on , τεύχεα (Homer) 
5. Causal, to make to sink , Lat. submergere, ἐμὲ καταδύουσι τῷ ἄχει (Xenophon Historicus); mostly in aor1, τοὺς γαυλοὺς καταδύσας (Herdotus Historicus); καταδῦσαι ναῦν to cut it down to the water's edge, disable it, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7843.definition:
1. in the mind or thoughts , (Odyssey by Homer); μηδέ τί τοι θάνατος κατ. ἔστω let not death sit heavy on thy heart , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. according to one's mind, satisfactory , (Theognis Elegiacus) (ML)

G7846.definition: to bend down , so as to be concave, (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically, μ. ἐλπίδας to bend down, overthrow hopes, (Euripides):—;Pass. to be bent (by intreaty), (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G7854.definition: to portion out :—;Mid. to receive as one's portion , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7859.definition:
1. to set in order, arrange , (Odyssey by Homer) (in Mid.); ἐπὶ νευρῇ κατακόσμει ὀϊστόν was fitting it on the string, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to fit out completely, adorn , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. to reduce to order , (Plutarch) (ML)

G7860.definition: to prevail over , τινός: absolute to prevail, gain the mastery , (Herdotus Historicus); of a name, to prevail, become current , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7861.definition:
1. to cover over, hide away, conceal , (Homer), etc. 
2. absolute to use concealment, to conceal oneself , of the gods, (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G7862.definition: Dep. to get for oneself entirely, gain possession of , and in past tenses, to have in full possession , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. (ML)

G7864.definition: to roll down :—;Pass. to be rolled down or thrown off , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7867.definition:
1. a seizing , ἐν καταλήψει within one's grasp , (Thucydides):—; an assaulting , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. a taking possession, occupation , (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)

G7871.definition:
1. Dep. to count up, number, reckon , (Xenophon Historicus); κ. τὸ εὐεργέτημα πρός τινα to put it down to his account , (Demosthenes Orator); καταλογιζέσθω μηδεὶς τοῦθ᾽ ὑμῖν ἐν ἀρετῇ let no one impute it to you as a virtue, (Aeschines Orator) 
2. to count or reckon among , Lat. annumerare, τοὺς ἀχαρίστους ἐν τοῖς ἀδίκοις (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7874.definition:
1. a dissolving, dissolution of governments, (Thucydides), etc. 
2. the dismissal or disbanding of a body of men, στρατιᾶς (Xenophon Historicus); εἰς κατάλυσιν till dismissal , of soldiers at a review, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. κ. τοῦ πολέμου an ending of the war, pacification , (Thucydides) 
4. generally, an end, termination , (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. a resting, lodging, rest , (Euripides) 
6. = κατάλυμα, a resting-place, guest-chamber, quarters, lodging , καταλύσιες (ionic for -λύσεις); (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G7875.definition:
1. to cut in pieces , (Lucian) 
2. to distribute , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G7877.definition: to mix up, mingle the ingredients , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G7879.definition:
1. to distribute, allot, assign , especially as pasture-land , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. to distribute, divide into separate bodies , (Xenophon Historicus):—;of a single person, κ. τινὰ εἰς τὴν τάξιν to assign him to his post, (Aeschines Orator) 
3. Mid. or Pass. to divide among themselves , (Thucydides) 
4. to occupy with cattle, to graze land , Lat. depasci, (Isocrates Orator):—;metaphorically to plunder , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

G7882.definition:
1. to card or comb well: to tear in pieces, rend in shreds , (Euripides); καταξαίνειν τινὰ εἰς φοινικίδα to pound him to red rags, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass., καταξανθείς crushed to atoms , (Sophocles Tragicus); πρὶν κατεξάνθαι (Euripides) 
2. to wear or waste away , Lat. atterere, (Aeschulus Tragicus): Pass., κατεξάνθην πόνοις, δακρύοις (Euripides) (ML)

G7887.definition:
1. to besprinkle or bespatter , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass., καταπαττόμενος (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. with accusative rei, to sprinkle or strew over , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G7891.definition: to mourn for, bewail , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G7893.definition:
1. to stick fast in the ground, plant firmly , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. Pass., with perfect and pluperfect active, to stand fast or firm in , (Iliad by Homer); absolute, στήλη καταπεπηγυῖα (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8240.definition:
1. very, very much, exceedingly , (Homer), etc. 
2. strengthening the word with which it stands, μάλα πολλά very many, (Homer); μάλα πάντες, μ. πᾶσαι, μ. πάντα, all together, every one , (Homer); μάλ᾽ ἀσκηθής all unhurt, (Odyssey by Homer); ἀβληχρὸς μάλα τοῖος so very weak, (Odyssey by Homer):—;so in attic, μάλα δὴ πρεσβύτης very old, (Xenophon Historicus); μ. γέ τινες ὀλίγοι (Plato Philosophus):—;so with Advs., πάγχυ μάλα and μάλα πάγχυ quite utterly, (Iliad by Homer); εὖ μάλα right well, (Odyssey by Homer); μάλ᾽ αἰεί for ever and aye, (Iliad by Homer); ἄχρι μάλα κνέφαος until quite dark, (Odyssey by Homer); μάλα διαμπερές right through, (Iliad by Homer):—;so in attic, to express repeated action, μάλ᾽ αὖθις, μάλ᾽ αὖ (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—; with Verbs, μή με μάλ᾽ αἴνεε praise me not greatly , (Iliad by Homer); ἡ δὲ μάλ᾽ ἡνιόχευεν she drove carefully , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. 
3. strengthening an assertion, εἰ μάλα μιν χόλος ἵκοι if wrath come on him ever so much , (Homer); so μάλα περ with a participle, μάλα περ μεμαώς though desiring never so much , (Iliad by Homer) 
4. in attic in answers, yes, certainly, exactly so , μάλα γε (Plato Philosophus), etc.; μ. τοι (Xenophon Historicus), etc.; καὶ μ. δή (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. comparative μᾶλλον, more , (Homer); μᾶλλον τοῦ δέοντος more than is right, (Plato Philosophus), etc.; παντὸς μᾶλλον more than anything, i. e. most certainly, (Plato Philosophus) 
6. denoting increase, more and more, still more , (Odyssey by Homer); μᾶλλον μᾶλλον, Lat. magis magisque, (Euripides) 
7. sometimes joined to a second comparative, ῥηίτεροι μᾶλλον (Iliad by Homer); μᾶλλον ἆσσον (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 
8. μᾶλλον δέ, much more , but rather , πολλοί, μᾶλλον δὲ πάντες (Demosthenes Orator) 
9. in μᾶλλον ἢ οὐ, οὐ seems redundant, ἥκει ὁ Πέρσης οὐδὲν μᾶλλον ἐπp ἡμέας ἢ οὐ ἐπp ὑμέας the Persians have come not more against us, than against you, (Herdotus Historicus); in this case μᾶλλον ἢ οὐ is preceded by another negative 
10. τὸ μ. καὶ ἧττον, a form of argument, which we call a fortiori , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
11. Sup. μάλιστα, most, most of all , (Homer), etc.; μάλιστα μέν . ., ἔπειτα δέ . ., first and above all . ., next . ., (Sophocles Tragicus):—; τί μάλιστ; what is the precise thing that you want? (Plato Philosophus); ὡς or ὅτι μ., Lat. quam maxime, (Plato Philosophus); ὅσον μ. (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὡς μ. certainly , in answers, (Plato Philosophus); ὡς δύναμαι μ. (Plato Philosophus); μακρῷ μ. (Herdotus Historicus) 
12. ἐς τὰ μάλιστα for the most part, mostly , (Herdotus Historicus); so, τὰ μάλιστα (Thucydides), etc.; also, ἀνὴρ δόκιμος ὁμοῖα τῷ μ. as famous as he that is most [famous, Refs 5th c.BC] 
13. ἐν τοῖς μ. especially, as much as any , (Thucydides) 
14. μάλιστα may be added to a Sup., ἔχθιστος μάλιστα, μάλιστα φίλτατος (Iliad by Homer); μ. φίλτατος (Euripides) 
15. with numbers, μάλιστα means about , (Thucydides), etc.; so, ἐς μέσον μάλιστα about the middle, (Herdotus Historicus); ἥμισυ μ. (Thucydides), etc. 
16. καὶ μάλιστα is used in answers, most certainly , Lat. vel maxime, (Aristophanes Comicus); so, μ γε (Sophocles Tragicus); μ. πάντων (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

4. adverb -μως, (Plato Philosophus): comparative -ώτερον (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8405.definition:
1. a feeding-place for cattle, pasture , (Homer); ν. ὕλης a woodland pasture , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. herbage , (Homeric Hymns):—;generally, food , (Hesiod) 
3. metaphorically, ἐπέων πολὺς νομός a wide range for words, (Iliad by Homer)

5. one of the districts into which Egypt was divided, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; applied also to other provinces , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8406.definition: ν. κοίτη a bed of sickness , (Euripides):—;adverb, νοσερῶς ἔχειν τὸ σῶμα (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8409.definition: carrying on the back : as Substantive a beast of burthen , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8410.definition: admonition, warning , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; τἀμὰ νουθετήματα given to me, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8412.definition: by night, nightly , Lat. nocturnus, (Aristophanes Comicus); ν. γενέσθαι to happen by night , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8413.definition: a bat , Lat. vespertilio, (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8422.definition: to make yellow or brown , by roasting or frying, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8423.definition:
1. belonging to a friend and guest, hospitable , Ζεὺς ξένιος as protector of the rights of hospitality , (Iliad by Homer):—; τράπεζα ξ. the guests' table, (Odyssey by Homer); ξένιός τινι bound to him by ties of hospitality , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. ξείνια, attic ξένια, ων, τά, friendly gifts, meat and drink , given to the guest by his host, (Homer); ξένια παρέσχε δαῖτα as a friendly gift , (Aeschulus Tragicus); βοῦν ξένια ἔπεμψεν (Xenophon Historicus); ἐπὶ ξένια καλεῖν to invite any one to eat with you , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; metaphorically, θάνατος ξένιά σοι γενήσεται (Euripides) 
3. foreign , (Pindar), attic (ML)

G8426.definition: a sword , (Homer); distinguished from μάχαιρα, q. see. (ML)

G8434.definition: a rasor , (Homer), etc.:—;proverb, ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἵσταται ἀκμῆς ὄλεθρος ἠὲ βιῶναι death or life is balanced on a rasor's edge, (Iliad by Homer); ἐπὶ ξυροῦ τῆς ἀκμῆς ἔχεται ἡμῖν τὰ πράγματα (Herdotus Historicus); βεβὼς ἐπὶ ξυρῷ τύχης (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8436.definition:
1. to scrape, plane, smooth or polish , (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically, ξῦσαι ἀπὸ γῆρας to scrape off, get rid of old age, (Homeric Hymns):—; Mid., παλτὸν ξύσασθαι to shape oneself a javelin-shaft, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. to make smooth, work delicately , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8437.definition:
1. a small spit , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
2. a coin stamped with a spit , (Plutarch) 
3. the leg of a compass , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8438.definition: an obol , as a weight, = 1/6th part of a δραχμή, worth rather more than three halfpence, (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐν δυοῖν ὀβολοῖν θεωρεῖν, as we might say "to sit in the shilling gallery, " (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8444.definition: a wayfarer, traveller , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;in (Iliad by Homer), a fellow-traveller , or guide. (ML)

G8445.definition:
1. to make or level a road , (Xenophon Historicus):—; Pass., of roads, to be made fit for use , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. metaphorically to reduce to a system , τι (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3. with dative pers. to act as pioneer, serve as guide , (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to make one's way, advance , Lat. progredi, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8447.definition:
1. to lament, bewail, mourn for : 
2. with accusative pers., (Homer); with accusative rei, ὁ δ᾽ ὀδύρετο πατρίδα γαῖαν mourned for it, i. e. for the want of it, (Odyssey by Homer); so, νόστον ὀδυρομένη (Odyssey by Homer) 
3. with genitive pers. to mourn for, for the sake of , (Homer) 
4. with dative pers. to wail or lament to or before others, (Homer) 
5. absolute to wail, mourn , (Homer) (ML)

G8448.definition: to steer , and so to guide, manage , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8449.definition:
1. kindred, relationship , (Herdotus Historicus), attic: intimacy, friendliness, kindness , (Thucydides):—;in plural friendly relations , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. of words, the proper sense , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8450.definition:
1. feminine of οἰκέτης, (Euripides) 
2. the mistress of the house , Lat. matrona, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8451.definition:
1. the act of dwelling, habitation , (Herdotus Historicus), attic

3. a house, dwelling, residence , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; κατασκαφὴς οἴκ. of the grave, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8453.definition:
1. an inhabitant , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; οἰκ. θεοῦ one who dwells in the temple of the god, (Euripides); Ἅιδου οἰκ., of one dead, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. a colonist , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8454.definition:
1. with accusative rei, to found as a colony or new settlement , πόλιν (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; Pass., πόλις οἴκισται (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. to people with new settlers, colonise , χώρην (Herdotus Historicus); νήσους (Thucydides):—;Mid. ὅπη γῆς πύργον οἰκιούμεθα in what part of the world we shall make ourselves a fenced home, (Euripides) 
3. with accusative pers. to remove, transplant , (Euripides); metaphorically, τὸν μὲν ἀφ᾽ ὑψηλῶν βραχὺν ὤικισεν brought him from high to low estate, (Euripides):—;Pass. to settle in a place, (Euripides) (ML)

G8456.definition: born in the house, homebred , of slaves, Lat. verna, (Plato Philosophus); of quails, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8457.definition:
1. the site of a house , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
2. the house itself, a building , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8459.definition:
pity, compassion , (Odyssey by Homer), Dht., attic:—;with genitive objecti, compassion for , οἶκτος τῆς πόλιος (Herdotus Historicus) 
the expression of pity, lamentation, piteous wailing , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;and in plural, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8460.definition:
1. pitiable, in piteous plight , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. of things, pitiable, piteous, lamentable , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
3. in active sense, piteous , (Odyssey by Homer); οἰκτρᾶς γόον ὄρνιθος, of the nightingale, (Sophocles Tragicus);—;neuter plural as regularly adverb οἰκτρῶς, (Aeschulus Tragicus) —;Besides comparative and Sup. οἰκτρότερος, -τατος, (Homer) has an irreg. Sup. οἴκτιστος (q. see.). (ML)

G8461.definition:
exclamation of pain, fright, pity, anger, grief, also of surprise, properly οἴ μοι ah me! woe's me! (Theognis Elegiacus);—;with genitive causae, οἴμοι τῶν κακῶν, οἴμοι γέλωτος ah me for my misfortunes, for the laughter, [variant datesTragica Adespota 
The last syllable in οἴμοι may be elided before ὡς. (ML)

G8464.definition: a can for ladling wine from the mixing bowl κρατήρ); into the cups, (Hesiod) (ML)

G8468.definition:
1. Dep. to be gone, to have gone , Lat. abesse (not abire) , in perfect sense, and imperfect ὠιχόμην in pluperfect sense, directly opposite to ἥκω, to have come , while ἔρχομαι, to go or come , serves as the present to both, (Homer), etc.;—;often with participle, οἴχεται φεύγων is fled and gone , (Iliad by Homer); ὤιχετ᾽ ἀποπτάμενος he hath taken flight and gone , (Iliad by Homer); οἴχεται θανών (see. infr. II. 1); also with an adjective, οἴχεται φροῦδος he's clean gone, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;with accusative pers. to have escaped from , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. Special usages, 
3. euphamistic for θνήσκω, to be gone hence , οἴχεται εἰς Ἀί̈δαο (Iliad by Homer); in attic, οἴχεται θανών (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—;participle οἰχόμενος for θανών, departed, dead , [variant datesTragica Adespota; but in (Homer) simply absent or away , Ὀδυσῆος πόθος οἰχομένοιο desire of the absent Ulysses, (Odyssey by Homer) 
4. to be undone, ruined , (Sophocles Tragicus); especially in ὤιχωκα or οἴχωκα, Lat. perii, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.

G8469.definition:
1. Dep. 
2. to take omens from the flight and cries of birds , Lat. augurium, capere, (Xenophon Historicus)

G8470.definition: divination by the flight or cries of birds , Lat. augurium, (Euripides) (ML)

G8472.definition:
1. a large bird, bird of prey , such as a vulture or eagle , and so distinguished from a common bird ὄρνις); (Homer), etc. 
2. a bird of omen or augury , (Homer), etc.:—;the flight to (not from) the right, i. e. towards the East, was fortunate, and vice versa. 
3. an omen, presage , drawn from these birds, Lat. auspicium or augurium , according as taken from seeing their flight or hearing their cry , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; δέκομαι τὸν οἰωνόν I accept the omen , hail it as favourable, (Herdotus Historicus)

(ML)

G8475.definition: eight thousand , (Herdotus Historicus); in singular, ἵππος ὀκτακισχιλίη "8000 horse, " (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8491.definition:
1. Act. = Lat. perdo,

7. of things, to be lost , (Homer)

G8500.definition: mostly in plural ὄλυραι, a kind of grain, spelt or rye , (Iliad by Homer); compare ζειά. (ML)

from ὁμόνους (ML)

ionic ὁμουρέω, future -ήσω to border upon, march with , [ οἱ Κελτοὶ, ὁμουρέουσι Κυνησίοισι (Herdotus Historicus) 
from ὅμορος (ML)

1. having the same borders with, marching with, bordering on , τοῖσι Δωριεῦσι, τῇ Λιβύῃ (Herdotus Historicus); absolute bordering , (Thucydides); πόλεμος ὅμορος a border war, (Demosthenes Orator)

G8515.definition: an unripe grape , πάροιθε δέ τ᾽ ὄμφακές εἰσιν (Odyssey by Homer); ὅτ᾽ ὄμφακες αἰόλλονται (Hesiod); ὅταν δὲ τεύχῃ Ζεὺς ἀπp ὄμφακος οἶνον, i. e. autumn, when the unripe grapes become fit to make wine, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8531.definition: hinder, belonging to the hinder part , Lat. posticus, τὰ ὀπ. σκέλεα the hind- legs, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8535.definition: a hoof, the solid hoof of the horse and ass, (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;after (Homer), like χηλή, the cloven hoof of horned cattle, (Homeric Hymns), etc. (ML)

G8536.definition:
1. heavy-armed, armed , δρόμος ὁπλ. a race of men in armour , opposite to the naked race, (Pindar); ὁπλ. στρατός an armed host, (Euripides); ὁπλ. κόσμος warrior- dress, armour, (Euripides)

1. to roast, broil , (Homer), etc.; with genitive partitive, ὀπτῆσαί τε κρεῶν to roast some meat, (Odyssey by Homer):—; ὀπτᾶν was used of cooking by means of fire or dry heat , opposite to ἕψω to boil in water , which never appears in (Homer); and a [variant datesComica Adespota poet remarks that Homer's heroes ate only roast meat:—;Pass., aor1 infinitive ὀπτηθῆναι (Odyssey by Homer)

4. metaphorically in Pass. to be burned by love, [Refs 3rd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina 
(ML)

G8545.definition:
1. an organ, instrument, tool, for making or doing a thing, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—;of a person, ἁπάντων ἀεὶ κακῶν ὄργ. (Sophocles Tragicus)

3. a musical instrument , (Plato Philosophus) 
4. a surgical instrument , (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. a work, product , λαί̈νεα Ἀμφίονος ὄργανα the stony works of Amphion, i. e. walls of Thebes, (Euripides) (ML)

G8546.definition:
1. to set straight :

5. (from signf. II) to guide aright , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὀρθ. ἀγῶνας to bring to a happy end , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὀ. βίον (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to succeed, prosper , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὸ ὀρθούμενον success , (Thucydides):—;of words and opinions, to be right, true , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν ἀγγέλωι κρυπτὸς ὀρθοῦται λόγος a secret message is rightly sent by messenger, not by letter, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
6. in Pass. also, to be upright, deal justly , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8547.definition:
1. a marking out by boundaries, limitation , (Aristotle Philosopher)

6. = ἕρμα 1, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

a branch , [variant datesAnthology Palantina

G8558.definition:
1. orphanhood , (Plato Philosophus)

(ML)

G8559.definition: to make holy, purify, set free from guilt by offerings , Lat. expiate, (Euripides):—;Mid., στόμα ὁσιοῦσθαι to keep one's tongue pure , not to speak profanely, (Euripides):—;Pass. to be purified , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8561.definition:
1. an earthen vessel , Lat. testa, (Aristophanes Comicus)

G8562.definition: to catch scent of, smell, scent, track , with genitive, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; absolute, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8564.definition:
1. nowhere , answering to πο; where? (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; with genitive, οὐδαμοῦ γῆς (Herdotus Historicus); οὐδαμοῦ ἦν φρενῶν (Euripides) 
2. οὐδαμοῦ λέγειν τινά to esteem as naught , Lat. nullo in loco habere, (Sophocles Tragicus); so, θεοὺς νομίζων οὐδ. (Aeschulus Tragicus); οὐδ. (or μηδαμοῦ); εἶναι, φαίνεσθαι, like Cicero's ne apparere quidem, not to be taken into account , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. of Manner, ἄλλοθι οὐδαμοῦ in no other way , (Plato Philosophus) 
(ML)

G8569.definition:
1. with a fair wind , Lat. vento secundo, οὔρ. πλοῦς, δρόμος a prosperous voyage, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. metaphorically prosperous, successful , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;neuter plural οὔρια as adverb, (Euripides) 
3. prospering, favouring, fair , of winds, (Euripides); comically of the bellows, οὐρίᾳ ῥιπίδι (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. οὐρία (i.e. πνοή); = οὖρος, a fair wind , οὐρίᾳ ἐφιέναι (i.e. ἑαυτόν); to run before the wind, (Plato Philosophus); so, ἐξ οὐρίων δραμοῦσα (i.e. δρόμων); after having run a fair course , (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀφήσω ἐμαυτὸν οὔριον (Aristophanes Comicus) 
5. Ζεὺς οὔριος, as sending fair winds , i. e. conducting things to a happy issue , [6th/5th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8573.definition: older form of ὄχθος, a rising ground, a bank, dyke by the side of a river, (Iliad by Homer): mostly in plural the raised banks of a river , (Homer); ὄχθαι καπέτοιο the banks of the trench, (Iliad by Homer); also the dunes or denes along the sea (compare θίς); (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8575.definition:
1. like ἐχυρός, firm, lasting, stout , (Hesiod) 
2. of places, strong, secure , (Euripides): especially of a stronghold or position, strong, tenable , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. adverb -ρῶς, (Euripides) (ML)

G8576.definition: to make fast and sure, fortify , (Polybius Historicus): —;the Mid. just like Act., (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8577.definition: to do, go or come late , (Xenophon Historicus):—; Pass., ὀψισθέντες belated, benighted , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8578.definition:
1. properly, cooked meat , or, generally, meat , opposite to bread and other provisions, (Homer) 
2. anything eaten with bread or food , to give it flavour and relish, κρόμυον, ποτῷ ὄψον onions, a zest or relish to wine, (Iliad by Homer); ἐσθίουσι ἐπὶ τῷ σίτῳ ὄψον (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. seasoning, sauce , (Plato Philosophus); κολλύραν καὶ κόνδυλον ὄψον ἐπ᾽ αὐτῇ pudding and knuckle- sauce withal, (Aristophanes Comicus); λιμῷ ὅσαπερ ὄψῳ διαχρῆσθε, i. e. "hunger is the best sauce," (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. generally, dainty fare , in plural dainties , (Plato Philosophus) 
5. at Athens, mostly, fish , the chief dainty of the Athenians, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
6. the fish-market , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8580.definition:
Πάγος, see: Ἄρειος.
Ἄρειος Πάυος (T, Ἄριος Π.), -ου, ὁ 
Hill of Pres or Mars, Areopagus; also, the Court of Areopagus, the highest tribunal of Athens: Act.17:19, 22.†
(AS)

G8583.definition:
1. a plaything, toy , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. in (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus), the Egyptians are called κακὰ παίγνια roguish playmates , 
3. a game, a sportive poem , [variant datesAnthology Palantina; of the merry chirp of the cicada, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8584.definition: a cake of preserved fruit , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8586.definition: to wrestle , (Iliad by Homer): π. τινί to wrestle with one, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., παλαισθείς beaten , (Euripides) (ML)

G8590.definition:
a concubine, mistress , Lat. pellex, opposite to a lawful wife κουριδίη ἄλοχος); (Homer) 
Prob. from same Root as παλλάς = νεᾶνις. (ML)

G8591.definition:
1. to poise or sway a missile before it is thrown, (Euripides) 
2. to sway other arms, not missiles, σάκος (Hesiod); πέλτας (Euripides):—;then, to toss a child, (Iliad by Homer); Νὺξ ὄχημm ἔπαλλεν she drave it furiously , (Euripides) 
3. κλήρους ἐν κυνέηι πάλλον they shook the lots together in a helmet, till one leapt forth, (Homer): absolute to cast lots , (Iliad by Homer); ὅθ᾽ αὐτοὺς οἱ βραβεῖς κλήροις ἔπηλαν where the stewards ranged them by casting lots, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Mid. to draw lots , ἔλαχον ἅλα παλλομένων I obtained the sea when we cast lots , (Iliad by Homer); so in (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. Pass. to swing or dash oneself , ἐν ἄντυγι πάλτο he dashed himself upon the shield-rim, (Iliad by Homer): to quiver, leap , especially in fear, πάλλεται ἦτορ (Iliad by Homer); also of the person, παλλομένη κραδίην (Iliad by Homer); of dying fish, to quiver, leap , (Herdotus Historicus) 
5. intransitive, like the Pass., to leap, bound , (Euripides): to quiver , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8593.definition: with the whole people, in a mass or body , (Herdotus Historicus); π. βοηθεῖν, στρατεύειν, of a whole people going out to war, a levee en masse , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8594.definition: to celebrate or attend a festival , πανηγύρις π. to keep holy-days , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8596.definition: with all the house, household and all , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8598.definition:
1. of every kind, of all sorts, manifold , (Homeric Hymns), etc.:—;in plural, πολλοὶ καὶ π. (Herdotus Historicus):—;adverb -πῶς, in all kinds of ways , Poeta quoted in (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. παντοδαπὸς γίγνεται, = παντοῖος γίγνεται, assumes every shape , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8599.definition:
1. the papyrus , an Egyptian rush with triangular stalks: paper was made by peeling off its outer coat βύβλος); and gluing the slips together. 
2. anything made of it, linen, cord , etc., [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8602.definition:
1. to look aside, take a side look , (Aristophanes Comicus); π. θατέρῳ (i.e. ὀφθαλμῷ); to look suspiciously with one eye, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to see wrong , (Lucian) (ML)

G8603.definition:
1. a message transmitted by beacons, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. an order, command , ἀπὸ παραγγέλματος by word of command , (Thucydides) 
3. an instruction, precept , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8606.definition:
1. a pattern or model of the thing to be executed, Lat. exemplar, an architect's plan , (Herdotus Historicus); a sculptor's or painter's model , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. a precedent, example , (Thucydides); ἐπὶ παραδείγματος by way of example , (Aeschines Orator) 
3. an example , i. e. a lesson or warning , π. ἔχειν τινός to take a lesson from another, (Thucydides); τὸ σὸν π. ἔχων (Sophocles Tragicus); ζῶντά τινα τοῖς λοιποῖς π. ποιεῖν (Demosthenes Orator) 
4. an argument, proof from example , (Thucydides) 
5. the model or copy of an existing thing, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8607.gloss: to hold forth as an example
G8607.definition:
1. to exhibit side by side : generally, to exhibit, bring forward , in Mid., (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. to represent as so and so, π. τινὰ οὐκ ὄντα (Polybius Historicus): also in bad sense, like παραδειγματίζω, (Plutarch) 
3. to exhibit and hand over , τί τινι (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8608.definition: to do an incredible thing; render notorious

G8609.definition: a running beside or over, traversing , (Plutarch); ἐν παραδρομῇ cursorily , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8611.definition: to heat to excess :—;Pass., aor1 participle παραθερμανθείς, of a man become quarrelsome in his cups, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8612.definition: juxta-position, neighbourhood , (Polybius Historicus); ἐκ παραθέσεως on comparison , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8614.definition:
1. to take away from beside, withdraw, remove , (Euripides):—; with genitive partitive to take away part of a thing, (Euripides):—;Pass., παρῃρημένοι τὰ ὅπλα having their arms taken from them, (Thucydides) 
2. π. ἀρὰν εἰς παῖδα to draw aside the curse on thy son's head, (Euripides) 
3. Mid. to draw over to one's own side, seduce, detach , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. to take away , (Xenophon Historicus): Mid., παραιρεῖσθαι τὴν θρασύτητα to lessen, damp it, (Demosthenes Orator) 
5. generally, to take away from, steal away from , τί τινος (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8615.definition: Dep. to be seated beside or near another, with dative, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

G8617.definition:
1. Dep. 
2. to order one to do a thing, advise, prescribe , τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; π. ταῦτα to give this advice , (Plato Philosophus);—;also, π. τινι, with infinitive, (Plato Philosophus) 
3. to exhort , τοιαῦτα παρακελευσάμενος having delivered this address , (Thucydides):—;absolute to encourage one another by shouting , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. παρακεκέλευστο in passive sense, orders had been given , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8621.definition:
1. to strike aside: to disappoint, mislead , (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass. to be led astray, go wrong , (Plato Philosophus):—;so also in Mid., (Isocrates Orator) 
2. in Mid. also, to strike away from oneself, parry , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8624.definition:
1. to make things alternate, to transpose , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. to change or alter a little , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. of Place, to pass by, go past, elude , (Xenophon Historicus):—; to get rid of , (Plutarch) 
4. to go beyond, exceed in point of time, (Plutarch) 
5. intransitive to pass by one another, to overlap , (Herdotus Historicus) 
6. to differ, vary , (Herdotus Historicus):—;impersonal, οὐ σμικρὸν παραλλάττει it makes no small difference , (Plato Philosophus) 
7. π. τοῦ σκοποῦ to go aside from the mark, (Plato Philosophus) 
8. to deviate from the course, to be liable to deviation , (Plato Philosophus); λόγοι παραλλάσσοντες delirious , (Euripides) 
9. to slip aside or away , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8625.definition: a loosening by the side: paralysis, palsy , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G8626.definition: to spend amiss, to waste, squander , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass., of persons, to be sacrificed uselessly , 3rd plural aor1 παραναλώθησαν (Plutarch) (ML)

G8627.definition:
1. acting contrary to law, lawless , (Euripides) 
2. of things, contrary to law, unlawful , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.:—;adverb, παρανόμως, illegally , (Thucydides) 
3. in attic law, παράνομα γράφειν, εἰπεῖν to propose an illegal measure , (Demosthenes Orator); παρανόμων γράφεσθαί τινα to indict one for proposing such a measure , (Demosthenes Orator): the indictment itself was παρανόμων γραφή (Aeschines Orator):—;in superlative, παρανομώτατα γεγραφότα (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8629.definition: a knife worn beside the sword, a dirk , (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G8630.definition:
1. altogether, absolutely , generally with Art., τὸ π. (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;with a negative, τὸ π. οὐδέν not at all , (Herdotus Historicus); οὔκ εἰμι τὸ π. ἄθεος (Plato Philosophus) 
2. in reckoning, ἐπὶ διηκόσια τὸ παράπαν up to two hundred altogether , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8631.definition: that which is spread before a thing, a hanging curtain , (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically a screen, cover , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8634.definition: a falling beside; κατὰ τὴν π. τινος in the course of an action, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8635.definition: to throw beside : metaphorically to run the risk of doing a thing, with participle, π. λαμβάνων (Sophocles Tragicus): to throw aside, reject , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8637.definition: to pass over in silence , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8638.definition:
1. a putting aside or away, banishing, relegatio , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2. a setting out things for sale, retail-trade , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3. παρίσταμαι); intransitive a being beside : 
4. a position or post near a king, (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. presence of mind, courage , (Polybius Historicus): also, desperation , (Polybius Historicus) 
6. as law-term, a small money deposit on entering law-suits, (Isaeus Orator) (ML)

G8641.definition:
1. to place side by side, draw up in battle-order , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;Mid. to draw up one's men in battle-order , (Xenophon Historicus); so of ships, (Thucydides):—;Mid. and Pass. to be drawn up along , παρατετάχατο παρὰ τὴν ἀκτήν (Herdotus Historicus); ἑκατέρωθεν παρατεταγμένοι (Thucydides); so, παρετάξαντο ἀλλήλοις (Xenophon Historicus): absolute, παρατεταγμένοι or παραταξάμενοι in order of battle , (Thucydides) 
2. in Mid. and Pass., also, to stand prepared , παρατετάχθαι πρὸς τὸ ἀποκρίνεσθαι (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8642.definition:
1. to run by or past , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to outrun, overtake , (Iliad by Homer): π. τὰ τότε κακά to go beyond, exceed them, (Euripides) 
3. to run through or over, run across (a space of ground expressed or implied), (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. to run over , i. e. treat in a cursory way , (Isocrates Orator):—; to slight, neglect , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
5. to escape unnoticed , τινά (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8645.definition:
1. to sit constantly beside, attend constantly, be always near , Lat. assidere, with dative, (Euripides) 
2. of judges, to be an assessor , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8647.definition: to stretch out in line , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8649.definition:
1. as preposition, 
2. with genitive loci, outside, before , παρὲκ λιμένος (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲξ ὁδοῦ out of the road, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. like χωρίς, besides, except, exclusive of , παρὲξ τοῦ ἀργύρου (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. with accusative out by the side of, along side of , παρὲξ ἅλα (Iliad by Homer); παρὲξ τὴν νῆσον away from the island, (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲξ δοῦρα out of the way of spears, (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲκ νόον out of sense and reason, foolishly, (Iliad by Homer); παρὲξ Ἀχιλῆα without the knowledge of Achilles, (Iliad by Homer) 
5. as adverb, 
6. of Place, out beside , στῆ δὲ παρέξ hard by , (Iliad by Homer); νῆχε παρέξ was swimming out along shore , (Odyssey by Homer) 
7. metaphorically beside the mark , παρὲξ ἀγορεύειν (Iliad by Homer) 
8. ἄλλα παρὲξ μεμνώμεθα let us talk of something else , (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲξ ἢ ὅσον except so long as, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8651.definition: marks of virginity; tokens of virginity

G8653.definition:
παρ-ιστάνω, see: παρίστημι.
παρ-ίστημι 
[in LXX for עָמַד, etc. ;] 
I. Transitive verb. in present tense., imperfect., future tense., 1 aorist.; 
1. to place beside, present, provide: with accusative, Act.9:41 23:24, 2Co.4:14, Col.1:28; with accusative and dative, Mat.26:53, Luk.2:22, Act.1:3 23:33, 1Co.8:8; before accusative pred., Rom.6:13, 16 (late pres., παριστάνετε), Rom.6:19 12:1, 2Co.11:2, Eph.5:27, Col.1:22, 2Ti.2:15. 
2. to present to the mind (cl.) : by argument, to prove (Xen., FlJ, al.), with accusative, Act.24:13. 
II. Intransitive. in perfect., pluperfect., 2 aorist.; 
1. to stand by or beside one : with dative of person(s), Act.1:10 9:39 23:2 27:23; ptcp., Mrk.14:47, 69-70 15:35, 39 Jhn.18:22 19:26. 
2. to appear: with nom. pred., before ἐνώπιον, Act.4:10; with dative of person(s), Act.27:24; so fut. mid. (of. LS, see word, B, ii, 2), Rom.14:10. 
3. to be at hand, be present, have come: Act.4:26 (LXX); of servants in attendance, ἐνώπιον τ. θεοῦ, Luk.1:19; absol., οἱ παρεστῶτες, Luk.19:24; before αὐτῷ, Act.23:2, 4; of time, Mrk.4:29 
4. to stand by for help or defence (Hom., Dem., Xen., al.): with dative of person(s), Rom.16:2, 2Ti.4:17.†
(AS)

G8654.definition:
1. to pass by , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
2. with accusative to go past , (Lucian) (ML)

G8657.definition:
1. to behave ill at wine, play drunken tricks , (Isaeus Orator) 
2. to act like a drunken man , (Plutarch); παροινήσας in a drunken fit , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. transitive to treat with drunken violence :—; Pass. to be so treated , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8659.definition:
1. to look at by the way, notice, remark , (Xenophon Historicus); τί τινι something in one, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. to overlook, disregard, neglect , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
3. to see amiss, see wrong , (Plato Philosophus) 
4. to look sideways , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8662.definition:
1. a peg on which to hang clothes, arms, etc., (Homer), etc.; ἀπὸ πασσαλόφι ζυγὸν ᾕρεον (Iliad by Homer); ἀπὸ πασσάλου αἴνυτο τόξον (Odyssey by Homer); ἐκ πασσαλόφι κρέμασεν φόρμιγγα (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. a gag , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8663.definition:
1. to sprinkle , φάρμακα πάσσων laying salves upon a wound, (Iliad by Homer): —;with genitive partitive, πάσσε ἁλός sprinkle some salt, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to besprinkle , χρυσῶι, ῥόδοις π. τινά (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. metaphorically to embroider, broider , (Iliad by Homer); π. ἀέθλους to work battles in embroidery , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8670.definition:
1. of or belonging to one's father , Lat. patrius, (Pindar), etc. 
2. = πατρικός, derived from one's fathers, hereditary , οἱπ. θεοί (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: —; τὰ πάτρια, Lat. instituta majorum, κατὰ τὰ πάτρια (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; rarely in singular, τὸ πάτριον παρείς neglecting the rule of our fathers , (Thucydides) Cf. πατρῷος. (ML)

G8672.definition: hoar-frost, rime , Lat. pruina, (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically, κουροβόρος π. the clotted blood of the eaten children, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8673.definition:
1. thickness , (Odyssey by Homer):—; absolute, πάχος in thickness , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. π. σαρκός stoutness , (Euripides) (ML)

G8674.definition:
1. thick, stout , (Homer):—; later, stout, fat , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. of things, thick, massive , (Homer):—;adverb -έως, roughly , of stating or arguing, (Aristotle Philosopher); παχύτερον or -έρως, (Plato Philosophus) 
3. of liquids, thick, curdled, clotted , (Iliad by Homer) 
4. οἱ παχέες the men of substance, the wealthy class , (Herdotus Historicus); τοὺς παχεῖς καὶ πλουσίους (Aristophanes Comicus) 
5. in [variant datesComica Adespota and Prose, thick-witted, gross, dull, stupid , like Lat. pinguis, crassus, [variant datesComica Adespota 
6. comparative παχύτερος, sup. -ύτατος:—;irregular comparative πάσσων, ον, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Sup. πάχιστος, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8675.definition:
1. to bind with fetters, to bind fast, make fast , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. to shackle, trammel, constrain , (Homer); with infinitive to constrain one to do a thing, (Homer) (ML)

G8676.definition:
a plain or flat , and collectively a plain flat open country , (Homer), etc. 
(ML)

G8677.definition:
1. on foot , πεζοί fighters on foot , opposite to horsemen, (Homer):—;also on land, going by land , opposite to sea-faring, (Homer):—;so, ὁ πεζὸς στρατός, or ὁ πεζός alone, sometimes foot-soldiery, infantry , opposite to cavalry ἡ ἵππος); (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. ὁ πεζός, also, a land-force or army , opposite to a naval force, (Herdotus Historicus); so, τὸ πεζόν (Herdotus Historicus); στρατιὰ καὶ ναυτικὴ καὶ πεζή (Thucydides); τὰ πεζὰ κράτιστοι strongest by land , (Thucydides) 
3. of animals, land , as opposite to birds and fishes, τὰ π. καὶ τὰ πτηνά beasts and birds, (Plato Philosophus) 
4. metaphorically of language, not rising above the ground, prosaic , (Lucian) 
5. dative feminine πεζῇ (entry ὁδῷ); as adverb, on foot , (Xenophon Historicus) 
6. by land , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8680.definition: a pirate , Lat. pirata, i. e. one who attacks ships, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8681.definition:
1. near, hard by, close , with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 
3. absolute, χριμφθεὶς πέλας (Odyssey by Homer); π. στείχειν, παρεῖναι, στῆναι [variant datesTragica Adespota 
4. οἱ πέλας (i.e. ὄντες); one's neighbours , (Thucydides), etc.: hence one's fellow-creatures, all men , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8683.definition: to hew or shape with an axe , Lat. dolare, (Odyssey by Homer) (in epic aor1 πελέκκησε), (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8685.definition:
1. an axe for felling trees, with two edges, opposite to the ἡμιπέλεκκον, (Homer) 
2. a sacrificial axe , (Homer)—;That it was not, properly, a battle axe appears from the phrase, οὐ δόρασι μάχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ καὶ πελέκεσι to fight not with spears only, but with common axes , i. e. to the last, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. in (Theophrastus Philosophus) Char., πέλεκυς as a child's nickname seems to mean a sharp blade. (ML)

G8688.definition: one who bears a light shield πέλτη); instead of the heavy ὅπλον, a targeteer , Lat. cetratus, (Euripides), etc. The peltasts held a place between the ὁπλῖται and ψιλοί. (ML)

G8689.definition:
1. a small light shield of leather without a rim ἴτυς); a target , Lat. cetra, originally used by the Thracians, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. a body of πελτασταί, (Euripides) 
3. a horse's ornament , (Euripides) 
4. = παλτόν, a shaft, pole , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8690.definition: a kind of axe , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

G8691.definition: any kind of dressed food; but mostly in plural, pastry, cakes, sweetmeats , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8692.definition: of or for mourning, mournful :—;adverb, πενθικῶς ἔχειν τινός to be in mourning for a person, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8694.definition:
1. Dep., used in present and imperfect : 
2. intransitive to work for one's daily bread ; generally, to toil, work, labour , (Homer) 
3. to be poor or needy , Solon , (Euripides), etc. 
4. with genitive to be poor in, have need of , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
5. transitive to work at, prepare, get ready , δαῖτα πένοντο (Odyssey by Homer); τί σε χρὴ ταῦτα πένεσθα; (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8695.definition:
1. five years old , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. of Time, lasting five years , (Thucydides):—; neuter adverb πεντάετες, for five years , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8696.definition: five cubits long or broad , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8705.definition: the commander of fifty men , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8708.definition:
1. fiftieth , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. as Substantive, ἡ πεντηκοστή, 
3. (i.e. μερίς); at Athens the duty of one-fiftieth , or two per century , on all exports and imports, (Isaeus Orator); εὕρηκε καινὴν ἱππικῆς τινὰ πεντηκοστήν he invented a new two per century duty , in lieu of his cavalry service, i. e. paid this instead of it, (Demosthenes Orator) 
4. (i.e. ἡμέρα); the fiftieth day (after the Passover), Pentecost , (New Testament) (ML)

G8709.definition:
1. ripe , Lat. maturus, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. metaphorically softened , ὀργή (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8711.definition:
1. of fruit, cooked by the sun, ripe, mellow , Lat. mitis, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. metaphorically in vocative, mostly as a term of endearment, kind, gentle , ὦ πέπον my good friend , (Iliad by Homer); κριὲ πέπον my pet ram, (Odyssey by Homer);—; in bad sense, soft, weak , (Iliad by Homer); ὦ πέπονες ye weaklings , (Iliad by Homer): —; μόχθος πέπων softened pain, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.: with dative, ἐχθροῖς π. gentle to one's foes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8712.definition:
1. to bring to an end, finish, accomplish, execute , [variant datesTragica Adespota, etc.:—;Pass. to be brought to an end, be finished , πάντα πεπείρανται (Odyssey by Homer): to be fulfilled, accomplished , (Euripides) etc.
