2. in speaking, to end a discourse, finish speaking, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
3. to repeat from beginning to end , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; to relate , (Euripides) 
4. absolute to effect one's purpose , especially with a negative, οὐδὲν π. to come to no issue, do no good, make no progress , (Euripides) 
5. intransitive to make way, reach or penetrate , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
6. intransitive to come to an end, end , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8717.definition: looked at from all sides, admired of all observers , (Euripides) (ML)

G8719.definition:
1. anything which is thrown round, a covering , (Plato Philosophus); χειρῶν περιβολαί embraces , (Euripides); so περιβολαί alone, (Xenophon Historicus); περιβολαὶ χθονός, i. e. the grave, (Euripides); π. [ ξίφεος] a scabbard, (Euripides): absolute of walls round a town, ἑπτάπυργοι π. (Euripides) 
2. a space enclosed, compass , οἰκίης μεγάλης περιβολή a house of large compass , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. a circumference, circuit , (Thucydides); π. ποιεῖσθαι to make a circuit , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. metaphorically, 
5. a compassing, endeavouring after , τῆς ἀρχῆς, Lat. affectatio imperii, (Xenophon Historicus) 
6. ἡ π. τοῦ λόγου the whole compass of the matter, long and short of it, (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

G8720.definition:
1. going round, compassing, encircling , (Euripides) 
2. as Substantive, περίβολος = περιβολή, ἐχίδνης περίβολοι the spires or coils of a serpent, (Euripides); in plural walls round a town , (Herdotus Historicus); so in singular, (Thucydides) 
3. an enclosure, circuit, compass , π. νεωρίων (Euripides); of a temple, the precincts , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8723.definition:
1. with two right hands , i.e. using both hands alike , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. very dexterous , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8724.definition: Dep. to grasp a thing with the hand , with genitive rei, (Plutarch) (ML)

G8725.definition:
1. to be around a place, with dative, (Thucydides); τὰ περιόντα circumstances , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. to be better than, superior to another, surpass, excel , with genitive, (Iliad by Homer); περίεσσι γυναικῶν εἶδός τε μέγεθός τε (Odyssey by Homer); οἳ περὶ μὲν βουλὴν Δαναῶν περὶ δd ἐστὲ μάχεσθαι λπαρr εθυαλσs μάχην)) (Iliad by Homer); with dative rei, σοφίᾳ π. τῶν Ἑλλήνων (Plato Philosophus): absolute to be superior , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἐκ περιόντος at an advantage , (Thucydides) 
3. to overlive, outlive , τινι (Herdotus Historicus): absolute to survive, remain alive , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;of things, to be extant, to be in existence , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. to be over and above, to remain in hand , of property, money, etc., (Thucydides); οἰόμενοι περιεῖναι χρήματά τῳ imagining that any one has a balance in his hands, (Demosthenes Orator) 
5. to be a result or consequence , περίεστιν ὑμῖν ἐκ τούτων what you have got by all this is . ., (Demosthenes Orator); τοσοῦτον ὑμῖν περίεστιν τοῦ πρὸς ἐμὲ μίσους you have so much hatred against me left , Philipp. quoted in (Demosthenes Orator); with infinitive, περίεστι ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς ἐρίζειν it remains for you to quarrel with them, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8726.definition: a girdle round the loins, apron , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8730.definition: to be seated or to sit all round , (Herdotus Historicus): of an army, to beleaguer, invest a town, (Herdotus Historicus); of ships, to blockade , (Herdotus Historicus): with accusative pers. to sit down by one, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8732.definition: to shear or clip all round , (Herdotus Historicus); Mid., περικείρεσθαι τρίχας to have one's hair clipt , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8736.definition:
1. to seize around, embrace , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. to encompass or surround an enemy, so as to intercept him, (Herdotus Historicus); μετεώρους τὰς ναῦς π. to intercept them at sea, (Thucydides); ἐπεὰν δὲ αὐτὸν περιλάβῃς when you get hold of him, catch him, (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to be caught , οἴμοι, περιείλημμαι μόνος (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. to comprehend, include , of a number of particulars, (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

G8740.definition: to go all round , with accusative, (Plutarch) (ML)

G8741.definition:
1. a going round, a flank march , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. a way round, the circumference, circuit, compass , τοῦ τείχεος, τῆς λίμνης (Herdotus Historicus); absolute, τὴν π. in circumference , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. γῆς π. a chart or map of the earth (compare πίναξ); (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. a going round in a circle, circuit , (Plutarch) 
5. of Time, a cycle or period of time , (Pindar), etc. 
6. a prescribed course of life, system , (Plato Philosophus) 
7. a fit of intermittent fever, (Demosthenes Orator) 
8. = περιφορά, a course at dinner , (Xenophon Historicus); π. λόγων table-talk , (Xenophon Historicus) 
9. the orbit of a heavenly body , (Xenophon Historicus) 
10. a well-rounded sentence, period , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8742.definition:
1. to build round , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. to enclose by building round , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be built up, walled in , (Thucydides); τὸ περιοικοδομημένον the space built round, the enclosure , Lat. ovile, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8745.definition:
1. a walking about, walking , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2. a place for walking, a covered walk , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. discourse during a walk, a philosophical discussion , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. οἱ ἐκ τοῦ περιπάτου the Peripatetics, school of Aristotle , because he taught walking in a περίπατος of the Lyceum at Athens, (Plutarch), etc. (ML)

G8746.definition:
1. to twine or enfold round :—;Pass. to fold oneself round , with dative, ἱστῷ περιπλεχθείς (Odyssey by Homer); absolute, δίκτυον εὖ μάλα περιπλεκόμενον close folding , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. to complicate, entangle , (Lucian) 
3. to wrap up in words , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8747.definition: a station for περίπολοι, a guard-house , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8748.definition: edged with purple , π. ἐσθής a robe with a purple border , the Roman toga praetextata or laticlavia , (Polybius Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8751.definition: to besprinkle all round , especially in sacred rites:—;Mid. to purify oneself , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G8753.definition: dry and hard all round, exceeding hard , of iron, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;metaphorically obstinate, stubborn , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8757.definition:
1. a standing round, a crowd standing round , Lat. corona, (Theophrastus Philosophus), etc. 
2. circumstances, a state of affairs , (Polybius Historicus):—;in bad sense, κατὰ τὰς π. in critical times , (Polybius Historicus) 
3. outward pomp and circumstance , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8758.definition:
1. to dress, clothe, wrap up , (Pindar); ἔπηξα δ᾽ αὐτὸν εὖ περιστείλας I planted the sword having wrapt it well with earth , i. e. planted it firmly , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. to dress or lay out a corpse, Lat. componere, (Odyssey by Homer), attic: simply, to bury , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. metaphorically to wrap up, cloak, cover , τἄδικ᾽ εὖ π. (Euripides):—;Mid., τὰ σὰ περιστέλλου κακά (Euripides) 
4. to take care of, protect, defend , (Herdotus Historicus); π. τοὺς νόμους to maintain the laws, (Herdotus Historicus); τὰ πάτρια (Demosthenes Orator); π. ἀοιδάν to uphold minstrelsy, (Pindar) (ML)

G8762.definition:
1. to whirl round , of one preparing to throw, (Homer); π. ἵππον to wheel it round , (Plutarch):—; Pass. to be turned round, spin round , (Iliad by Homer); π. εἰς τἀληθῆ to come round to it, (Plato Philosophus) 
2. π. τὼ χεῖρε to tie his hands behind him, (Lysias Orator). (ML)

G8763.definition:
1. with pillars round the wall, surrounded with a colonnade , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. as Substantive, περίστυλον, ου, τό, or περίστυλος, ὁ, a peristyle, colonnade round a temple or court-yard , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8764.definition:
1. to drag about , ἄνω καὶ κάτω (Lucian) 
2. to tear away from , τί τινος (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8765.definition:
1. to slit and tear off , (Plutarch) 
2. Pass., of a river, περισχίζεσθαι τὸν χῶρον to split round a piece of land, i. e. split into two branches so as to surround it, (Herdotus Historicus);—;so, of a stream of men, to part and go different ways , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8766.definition:
1. to wall all round , πλίνθοις Βαβυλῶνα (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to surround with a wall , so as to beleaguer, (Thucydides) 
3. to build round , ὁ περιτετειχισμένος κύκλος (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8768.definition:
1. the line round a circular body, a periphery, circumference , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. the outer surface , (Plutarch) 
3. a round body , (Plutarch) 
from περιφερής (ML)

G8769.definition:
1. moving round, surrounding , with genitive, (Euripides) 
2. surrounded by , with dative, (Euripides) 
3. round, circular , (Plato Philosophus):—;of bodies, spherical, globular , (Plato Philosophus):—;of style, rounded , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8770.definition:
1. meats carried round , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. a going round, rotatory motion, circuit, revolution , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
3. the revolving vault of heaven, (Plato Philosophus) 
4. metaphorically, ἐν ταῖς περιφοραῖς in society , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8773.definition: to surround with a stockade , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8774.definition: exceeding joyous or glad , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τινι at a thing, (Herdotus Historicus):—; τὸ π. excessive joy , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8775.definition: to pour round or over , τί τινι, properly of liquids, (Homer); of metal-workers, χρυσὸν κέρασιν περιχεύας having spread gold leaf round its horns, (Iliad by Homer); so in Mid., ὡς δ᾽ ὅτε τις χρυσὸν περιχεύεται ἀργύρῳ (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass. to be poured around , περὶ δ᾽ ἀμβρόσιος κέχυθ᾽ ὕπνος (Iliad by Homer); τῶν ὀστέων περικεχυμένων heaped all round , (Herdotus Historicus); of persons, περιχυθέντες crowding round , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8778.definition:
1. to soften, ripen or change , by means of heat: 
2. of the sun, to ripen fruit, (Odyssey by Homer); compare πεπαίνω. 
3. by the action of fire, to cook, dress, bake , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., (Herdotus Historicus):—;Mid., πέσσεσθαι πέμματα to cook oneself cakes, (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. of the stomach, to digest , like Lat. concoquere, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
5. metaphorically, χόλον πέσσειν to cherish or nurse one's wrath, Lat. fovere, (Iliad by Homer); βέλος πέσσειν to have a dart in one to nurse , (Iliad by Homer); but in good sense, γέρα πεσσέμεν to enjoy them, (Iliad by Homer); also, ἀκίνδυνον αἰῶνα πέσσειν to lead a sodden life of ease, (Pindar) (ML)

G8779.definition:
1. a leaf , mostly in plural, (Homer):—; poetry, νεικέων πέταλα contentious votes (compare πεταλισμός); (Pindar) 
2. a leaf of metal , (Lucian) (ML)

G8780.definition: to spread out sails or clothes, (Odyssey by Homer); χεῖρε πετάσσας, of one swimming, (Odyssey by Homer): metaphorically, θυμὸν πετάσαι to open one's heart, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., mostly in perfect, to be spread on all sides , (Homer): participle spread wide, opened wide , of folding doors, πύλαι πεπταμέναι (Iliad by Homer); πετάσθησαν (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8781.definition:
a perch for fowls to roost at night, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G8783.definition:
1. throwing stones , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. as Substantive, πετροβόλος, an engine for throwing stones , Lat. ballista, (Polybius Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8784.definition:
1. the pine , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. any thing made from its wood, a torch of pine-wood , [variant datesTragica Adespota 
3. a writing-tablet , (Euripides) (ML)

G8785.definition: of or from pine or pine-wood , (Sophocles Tragicus); π. δάκρυα tears of the pine , i. e. the resinous drops that ooze from it, (Euripides) (ML)

G8787.definition:
1. anything joined together, framework , of a ship, [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Lat. pegma, a moveable scaffold used in theatres, (Juvenal) 
2. metaphorically, π. γενναίως παγέν a bond in honour bound, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. π. τῆς χιόνος frozen snow, (Polybius Historicus) 
(ML)

G8788.definition:
1. to leap, spring, bound , ὑψόσε ποσσὶν ἐπήδα (Iliad by Homer); π. ἐς σκάφος (Sophocles Tragicus); with accusative cognate, πήδημα πηδᾶν to take a leap, (Euripides); with accusative loci, πεδία πηδᾶν to bound over them, (Sophocles Tragicus); π. πλάκα (Euripides) 
2. metaphorically of an arrow, (Iliad by Homer); of the heart, to leap, throb , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; of sudden changes, τί πηδᾶις εἰς ἄλλους τρόπου; (Euripides) (ML)

G8789.definition: of clay , Lat. fictilis, οἱ πήλινοι clay figures , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8790.definition:
1. to make fat, fatten , (Euripides); π. χθόνα to fatten the soil, of a dead man, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass. to be or become fat , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2. metaphorically, 
3. to increase, enlarge , πλοῦτον (Pindar) 
4. to make wanton, excite , (Aeschulus Tragicus): —;Pass. to wax fat and wanton , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἔχθεσιν πιαίνεσθαι to batten on quarrels, (Pindar) (ML)

G8791.definition:
an ape, monkey , (Aristophanes Comicus); as feminine, πίθηκος μήτηρ (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor):—;of persons, an ape, jackanapes , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G8792.definition:
πιθός, see: πειθός.
πειθός (πιθός, WH), -ή, -όν 
(πείθω), = cl. πιθανός, 
persuasive: 1Co.2:4 (not found elsewhere).†
(AS)

G8796.definition: pitch , Lat. pix, (Iliad by Homer), etc.: proverbial, ἄρτι μῦς πίττης γεύεται, i. e. he has got the first taste of misery, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8797.definition: the pine, stone pine , (Homer):—;proverbial, πίτυος τρόπον ἐκτρίβεσθαι to be destroyed like a pine , i. e. utterly , because the pine when cut down never grows again, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8798.definition:
1. neuter πῖον, genitive πίονος, fat, plump , Lat. pinguis, (Homer); π. δημός rich fat, (Iliad by Homer); of oil, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. of soil, fat, rich. (Iliad by Homer); also, πίονα ἔργα pingues segetes , (Iliad by Homer); ὀπώρας πίων ποτός, of wine, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. of persons and places, rich, wealthy , (Homer); πίονι μέτρῳ in plenteous measure, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
4. The comparative and Sup. are πι-ότερος, πι-ότατος, as if from πῖος. (ML)

G8799.definition: to turn sideways or aside , πλ. πρὸς τοὺς ἀντίους ἀνέμους (i.e. τὴν ναῦν); to beat up against adverse winds, (Lucian): metaphorically, πλ. ἢ φωνὴν ἢ πρᾶξιν to adapt them to circumstances , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8800.definition:
1. placed sideways, slanting, aslant , Lat. obliquus, (Thucydides) 
2. πλάγια, ων, τά, the sides , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in military sense, τοῖς πλαγίοις ἐπιέναι to attack the flanks , (Thucydides); εἰς τὰ πλ. παράγειν or παραπέμπειν to make an army file off right and left , (Xenophon Historicus); πλαγίους λαβεῖν τοὺς πολεμίους to take the enemy in flank , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. with Preps. in adverbial sense, εἰς πλάγιον obliquely , (Xenophon Historicus); εἰς τὰ πλάγια, opposite to εἰς τὸ ἀντίον, (Thucydides); ἐκ πλαγίου in flank , (Thucydides); κατὰ πλάγια (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. metaphorically not straightforward, crooked, treacherous , φρένες (Pindar); πλάγια φρονεῖν (Euripides) (ML)

G8801.definition: a making to wander, a dispersing , τῶν νεῶν (Thucydides) (ML)

G8802.definition:
the oriental plane , Lat. platanus, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
From πλατύς, because of its broad leaves. (ML)

G8804.definition: mostly, most often, very often , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8805.definition: more frequently, oftener , (Plato Philosophus): several times, frequently , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8809.definition:
1. an advantage, gain, privilege , (Plato Philosophus): in plural gains, successes , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. an act of overreaching, selfish trick , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8810.definition:
1. a rib : mostly in plural the ribs, the side , (Iliad by Homer), etc.;—;also in singular, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. of places, πλευρὸν νεῶν the side of the bay where the ships lay, (Sophocles Tragicus); τὸ δεξιὸν πλ. the right flank (of an army), (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8811.definition:
a mistake in music, false note : metaphorically a fault, offence, error , (Plato Philosophus) 
from πλημμελέω (ML)

G8812.definition: to make a false note in music : metaphorically to go wrong, offend, err , τι in a thing, (Euripides), etc.; εἴς τινα (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass., πλημμελεῖσθαι ὑπό τινος to be ill-treated by one, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8815.definition:
1. a filling up, filling , (Plato Philosophus): often of eating and drinking, satiety , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. the completion of a number , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8816.definition:
1. near, close to , with genitive or dative, πλησίοι ἀλλήλων or ἀλλήλοισι (Homer):—;absolute near, neighbouring , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;as Substantive a neighbour , ἰδὼν ἐς πλ. ἄλλον (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. adverb πλησίον, doric πλα_τίον, = πέλας, near, nigh, hard by , with genitive, (Homer), etc.; with dative, (Euripides) 
3. with the Art., ὁ πλησίον (i.e. ὤν); one's neighbour , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; so in doric, ὁ πλα_τίον (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus):—;also, with Substantives, ὁ πλ. παράδεισος (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. comparative πλησιαίτερος, Sup. -αίτατος, (Xenophon Historicus)—;comparative adverb πλησιαιτέρω, (Herdotus Historicus); -αίτερον, (Xenophon Historicus); Sup. -αίτατα, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8818.definition:
1. to make into bricks , τὴν γῆν (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute to make bricks , (Aristophanes Comicus);—;so in Mid., thuc. 
2. to build of brick , τείχη (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. to make in the form of a plinth or brick , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
(ML)

G8819.definition:
1. a small brick , (Thucydides) 
2. = πλαίσιον, a rectangle or square , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8820.definition: a brick , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; πλίνθους ἑλκύσαι, εἰρύσαι, Lat. ducere lateres, to make bricks , (Herdotus Historicus); ὀπτᾶν to bake them, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8822.definition:
1. a twining: anything woven, a web , (Euripides) 
2. metaphorically the complication of a plot, opposite to λύσις, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8824.definition:
1. floating , (Odyssey by Homer); πλωτοί swimmers , i. e. fish, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. navigable , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. of seasons, fit for navigation , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8827.definition: the organ of breathing, the lungs , Lat. pulmo, (Iliad by Homer): mostly in plural, [variant datesTragica Adespota; πνεῦμ᾽ ἀνεὶς ἐκ πλευμόνων (Euripides) (ML)

G8828.definition:
1. grass, herb , (Homer), etc.; ποία Μηδική, Lat. herba Medica, sainfoin or lucerne , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. the grass , i. e. a grassy place , plat., (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. in Poets, of Time, τέσσαρας πόας four grasses , i. e. summers , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8829.definition:
1. to long for, yearn after what is absent, to miss or regret what is lost, Lat. desiderare, (Homer), etc.; ποθεῖς τὸν οὐ παρόντα (Aristophanes Comicus); π. τὰς ἐν τῆι νεότητι ἡδονάς (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass., ὦ ποθουμένη (i.e. Εἰρήνη) (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. of things, to require , ποθεῖ ἡ ἀπόκρισις ἐρώτησιν τοιάνδε (Plato Philosophus) 
3. with infinitive to be anxious to do, (Euripides); τὸ νοσοῦν ποθεῖ σε ξυμπαραστάτην λαβεῖν my sickness needs to take thee as an assistant, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. absolute, τὸ ποθοῦν one's desiring, one's longing , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
5. as Dep., ποθουμένη φρήν the longing soul, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8830.definition:
1. a marking with various colours, embroidering, embroidery , (Plato Philosophus): in plural pieces of broidery , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. varied aspect, diversity , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. versatility, subtlety, craft , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8831.definition:
1. to work in various colours, to broider, work in embroidery , (Euripides); χορὸν ποίκιλλε he wrought a χορός of cunning workmanship , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to embroider a robe, (Pindar), etc. 
3. generally, to diversify, vary , (Euripides):—;of style, to embellish , (Pindar):—; to speak as in riddles , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8832.definition:
1. a broidered stuff, brocade , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. broidered work, broidery , (Homer) 
3. generally, a variety, diversity , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8837.definition: of or for a shepherd , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): —; ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8838.definition:
1. wool in its raw state, a fleece , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: a lock or tuft of wool , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. proverbial in heterocl. accusative of 3rd declension, εἰς ὄνου πόκας to an ass shearing , i. e. to no-place, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8839.definition:
1. of or for war , (Thucydides); ἀσπὶς πολεμικωτάτη most fit for service , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); the art of war, war , (Plato Philosophus): —; τὰ πολεμικά warlike exercises , (Thucydides) 
3. τὸ πολεμικόν the signal for battle , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. the military class , opposite to the civilian, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
5. of persons, skilled in war, warlike , (Thucydides), etc. 
6. like an enemy, stirring up hostility , (Xenophon Historicus):—;adverb, πολεμικῶς ἔχειν to be hostile , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8840.definition:
1. of or belonging to war , (Pindar), etc.: —; τὰ πολέμια whatever belongs to war, war and its business , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. of or like an enemy, hostile , (Pindar), etc.:—;as Substantive an enemy , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; οἱ π. the enemy , (Thucydides): —; τὸ π. hostility , (Thucydides) 
3. generally, opposed, adverse , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. of or from the enemy , (Aeschulus Tragicus); πολέμια, ων, τά, enemy's wares, contraband , (Aristophanes Comicus): —; ἡ πολεμία (i.e. γῆ, χώρα); the enemy's country , (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. adverb -ίως, in hostile manner , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8841.definition:
1. a warrior, combatant , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. π. ἵππος a war-horse, charger , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8843.definition:
1. to hem in a city, blockade, beleaguer, besiege , (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;Pass. to be besieged, in a state of siege , (Herdotus Historicus); of Scamander, to be dammed back , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. metaphorically to be besieged, pestered , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8844.definition:
1. a besieging, siege , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. metaphorically a besieging, pestering , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8845.definition:
1. gray, grizzled, grisly , of wolves, of iron, of the sea, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. mostly of hair, gray or hoary from age, (Homer); πολιοί gray-haired men , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;absolute, αἱ πολιαί (i.e. τρίχες); (Pindar); ἅμα ταῖς πολιαῖς κατιούσαις as the gray hairs come down (i.e. from the temples to the beard), (Aristophanes Comicus); π. δάκρυον ἐμβαλών an old man's tear, (Euripides) 
3. metaphorically hoary, venerable , (Euripides) 
4. like λευκός, bright, clear, serene , (Hesiod) (ML)

G8847.definition:
1. one of many , Lat. unus e multis, i.e. the smallest, least , (Thucydides), etc.:—; adverb, δευτέρως καὶ πολλοστῶς in a very small degree , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. of Time, πολλοστῷ χρόνῳ after a very long time , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8856.definition:
1. much-tangled, thick-wreathed , of a serpent's coils, (Euripides); of the polypus, with tangled, twisting arms , (Theognis Elegiacus) 
2. metaphorically much-twisting, complex, intricate , [Refs 5th c.BC, 5th/4th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8860.definition:
1. long-existing, of olden time, ancient , (Homeric Hymns) 
2. lasting for long , (Aristotle Philosopher):—;comparative -ώτερος, (Plato Philosophus); Sup. -ώτατος, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8861.definition: to be very careful , opposite to ὀλιγωρέω, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8862.definition:
1. in early Greek only as Dep. 
2. absolute to work hard, do work, suffer toil , (Homer); περὶ δόρπα πονέοντο were busied about their supper, (Iliad by Homer); so, πεπόνητο καθ᾽ ἵππους was busy with the horses, of a charioteer, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. metaphorically to be in distress, to distress oneself , (Iliad by Homer):—; to suffer, be sick , (Thucydides) 
4. with accusative to work hard at, to make or do with pains or care , (Homer) 
5. after (Homer), the active form prevails 
6. intransitive to toil, labour , (Theognis Elegiacus), attic; μάτην π. to labour in vain, (Sophocles Tragicus); with accusative, τὰ μηδὲν ὠφελοῦντα μὴ πόνει do not labour at things that profit not, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
7. with accusative cognate, π. πόνον, μόχθους to go through, suffer them, [variant datesTragica Adespota; also with accusative partis, πονεῖν τὰ σκέλη (Aristophanes Comicus) 
8. absolute to labour, be hard-pressed, suffer , (Thucydides): to be worn out, spoilt , (Demosthenes Orator) 
9. Pass., impersonal, οὐκ ἄλλως αὐτοῖς πεπόνηται = πεπονήκασι, (Plato Philosophus) 
10. transitive, 
11. with accusative pers. to afflict, distress , (Pindar):—;Pass. to be worn out, to suffer greatly , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
12. Pass., also, to be trained or educated , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
13. with accusative rei, like ἐκπονεῖν, to gain by toil or labour , χρήματα (Xenophon Historicus): Pass. to be won or achieved by toil , (Pindar) (ML)

G8863.definition: Dep. to be evil, act wickedly, play the rogue , (Aristotle Philosopher); οἱ πεπονηρευμένοι (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8864.definition:
to pass the sea , νῆυς ποντοποροῦσα sea-sailing , (Odyssey by Homer) 
from ποντοπόρος (ML)

G8866.definition: a house of ill-fame, brothel , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8867.definition: of or for harlots , π. τέλος the tax paid by brothel-keepers , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8869.definition:
1. a purple garment or covering , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. a red-coloured bird , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8874.definition: drinking, a drinking-bout, carousal , (Xenophon Historicus); παρὰ πότον, Lat. inter pocula, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν τοῖς πότοις (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8876.definition: a selling, sale , ὠνῇ τε καὶ πρήσι (ionic dative) χρέονται (Herdotus Historicus); ἐπὶ πρήσι for sale , (Herdotus Historicus); πρᾶσιν ποιεῖσθαι (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8879.definition:
1. to make soft, mild or gentle, to soften, soothe, calm , (Hesiod), etc.; πρ. ἕλκος to soothe a raging sore, (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. τινὰ λόγοις (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass. to become soft or gentle, grow milder , (Herdotus Historicus); of passion, to abate , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. to tame wild animals, (Hesiod) (ML)

G8880.definition:
1. a gift of honour , such as was offered to elders, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. the privilege of age , and generally, a privilege , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
3. the right of the eldest, his share of the inheritance , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8881.definition:
1. an old man , Lat. senex, (the prose form is πρεσβύτης); (Sophocles Tragicus):—; ὁ πρέσβυς is used much like ὁ πρεσβύτερος, the elder , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;plural πρέσβεις, elders , always implying dignity, chiefs, princes , (Aeschulus Tragicus); epic πρέσβηες (Hesiod) 
2. (Homer) uses only the comparative and Sup., comparative πρεσβύτερος, α, ον, elder, older , (Iliad by Homer), attic; ἐνιαυτῷ by a year, (Aristophanes Comicus); βουλαὶ πρεσβύτεραι the wise councils of age , (Pindar);—;Sup. πρεσβύτατος, η, ον, eldest , (Iliad by Homer), etc.: —;the comparative and Sup. were used of things, πρεσβύτερόν τι (or οὐδὲν); ἔχειν = Lat. aliquid (or nihil) antiquius habere, to deem higher, more important , τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ πρεσβύτερα ποιεῖσθαι ἢ τὰ τῶν ἀνδρῶν (Herdotus Historicus); πρεσβύτατον κρίνειν τι (Thucydides); πρεσβυτέρως γυμναστικὴν μουσικῆς τετιμηκέναι more highly than . . , (Plato Philosophus): —;hence, merely of magnitude, πρεσβύτερον κακὸν κακοῦ one evil greater than another, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. like πρεσβευτής, an ambassador , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—;plural πρέσβεις is more used than πρεσβευταί, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
4. a chief, president : comparative πρεσβύτερος, an elder of the Jewish Council , (New Testament), etc.: an elder of the Church, presbyter , (New Testament) (ML)

G8882.definition:
1. to blow up, swell out by blowing , ἔπρησεν δ᾽ ἄνεμος μέσον ἱστίον (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. to blow out, drive out by blowing , τὸ δ᾽ [ αἷμα] ἀνὰ στόμα πρῆσε he blew a shower of blood through his mouth, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8883.definition:
1. to have a thing sold to one, to buy, purchase , (Homer), attic; with dative pretii, πρ. κτεάτεσσιν ἑοῖσιν to buy with one's money, (Odyssey by Homer); with genitive, πρ. θανάτοιο to purchase by his death, (Pindar); πρ. τι ταλάντου (Xenophon Historicus); π. πολλοῦ (Xenophon Historicus); metaphorically, οὐδενὸς λόγου πρίασθαι to buy at no price, (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. τι παρά τινος (Herdotus Historicus):—; πρ. τίμιον τοὔλαιον to buy it dear, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to farm a tax, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8886.definition:
1. a choosing one thing before another, an act of deliberate choice, a purpose, resolution , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—; κατὰ προαίρεσιν on purpose, as one will , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. a purpose, plan , or scope of action, a course of life, principle of action, (Demosthenes Orator) 
3. in political language, a deliberate course of action, a policy , (Demosthenes Orator):—;also, a mode of government, such as an oligarchy, (Demosthenes Orator); in plural, τὰς κοινὰς πρ. your public principles, your general policy , (Demosthenes Orator) 
4. a department of government , (Demosthenes Orator) 
5. a political party , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8890.definition: the space immediately in front of or round a town, a suburb , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8891.definition: property in cattle πρόβατα); cattle , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8892.definition:
1. anything projecting, a headland, promontory , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. anything put before one, a fence, barrier, screen , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; πρ. σώματος, of a shield, (Aeschulus Tragicus); προβλήματα ἵππων χαλκᾶ the brasen armour of horses, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. with genitive a defence against a thing, πέτρων (Aeschulus Tragicus); χείματος (Euripides); κακῶν (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. πρ. φόβου ἢ αἰδοῦς ἔχειν to have fear or shame as a defence , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
5. anything put forward as an excuse or screen , (Demosthenes Orator); so, πρ. λαβεῖν τινά (as we say) to make a stalking horse of him, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6. that which is proposed, a task, business , (Euripides) 
7. a problem in Geometry, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8894.definition:
1. to be ready, willing, eager, zealous to do a thing, with infinitive, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; also πρ. ὅπως (Herdotus Historicus), attic 
2. absolute to shew zeal, exert oneself , (Herdotus Historicus):—; to be of good cheer , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. with accusative rei, to be eager or zealous for, promote eagerly, desire ardently , (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

G8895.definition:
1. the front-door, the door leading from the αὐλή, (Homer); also in plural, (Homer) 
2. the space before a door , a kind of porch or verandah , Lat. vestibulum, (Odyssey by Homer), attic 
3. metaphorically, Κόρινθος πρόθυρον Ποτειδᾶνος (Pindar); πρόθυρα ἀρετῆς (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8896.definition:
1. to send before, send on or forward , (Homer): also, to send something to another, ἀγγελίας, φήμην (Odyssey by Homer):—; (Homer) often with an infinitive added; αἰετὼ προέηκα πέτεσθαι, οὖρον προέηκεν ἀῆναι (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. to send away, dismiss, let go , (Iliad by Homer); τήνδε θεῷ πρόες let her go to the god, i. e. in reverence to him, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. to let loose, let fall , especially thoughtlessly, ἔπος προέηκε let drop a word, (Odyssey by Homer); πηδάλιον ἐκ χειρῶν προέηκε he let the helm slip from his hands, (Odyssey by Homer); δάκρυα προῆκεν (Euripides) 
4. of missiles, to send forth, shoot or dart forth , (Homer) 
5. of a river, ὕδωρ προί̈ει ἐς Πηνειόν it pours its water into the Peneius, (Iliad by Homer) 
6. πρ. τινί ποιεῖν τι to allow one to do, (Pindar) 
7. to give up, deliver over, betray one to his enemy, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Pass. to be given or thrown away , εἰ προεῖτο ταῦτα (Demosthenes Orator) 
8. ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτίκα ἡδὺ πρ. αὑτόν to give up or devote oneself to present delights, (Xenophon Historicus) 
9. Mid. to send forward from oneself, drive forward , (Xenophon Historicus):—;of sounds, to utter , (Aeschines Orator), etc. 
10. to give up, let go: to give up to the enemy, (Thucydides), etc.; πρ. σφᾶς αὑτούς gave themselves up as lost , (Thucydides) 
11. to desert, abandon , (Thucydides); οὐδαμῆ προί̈εντο ἑαυτούς did not lose themselves (i. e. take bribes), (Demosthenes Orator) 
12. to give away, give freely , (Thucydides), etc.; προέσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων (Demosthenes Orator) 
13. to throw off one's clothes, (Demosthenes Orator): and, in bad sense, to throw away , τὸν καιρόν (Demosthenes Orator); τὰ πατρῷα (Aeschines Orator): absolute to be lavish , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
14. a second predicate is sometimes added, ἡμᾶς προέσθαι ἀδικουμένους to suffer us to be wronged, (Thucydides); προέμενοι αὐτοὺς ἀπολέσθαι (Xenophon Historicus); πρ. τινὶ ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατῆσαι (Demosthenes Orator) 
15. to suffer to escape , (Polybius Historicus) 
16. rarely in good sense, to give over to one, confide to one's care , (Xenophon Historicus) 
17. to neglect, disregard , (Aristotle Philosopher):—; absolute to neglect all advice, to be reckless , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8897.definition:
1. to set before; so in Mid., (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. Pass., with aorist2 and perfect active, φυλακῆς μὴ προκαθεστηκυίας no guard having been set beforehand , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8898.definition:
1. to seize beforehand, preoccupy , (Thucydides), etc.:—;Pass. to be preoccupied , (Thucydides) 
2. metaphorically to anticipate, frustrate , (Thucydides):—;of persons, to anticipate or surprise them, (Thucydides) 
3. to overpower before , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8902.definition: to go out for foraging , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8903.definition:
1. a foraging, a foraging expedition, foray , (Xenophon Historicus): in plural, foraging parties , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. an elephant's trunk , (Polybius Historicus) 
3. = προ-νομία, (Lucian) (ML)

G8904.definition:
1. an opening or introduction to a thing; in Music, a prelude, overture , (Pindar); in poems and speeches, a proem, preface, preamble, introduction , Lat. exordium, (Pindar) 
2. metaphorically of any prelude or beginning , φροίμιον χορεύσομαι (Aeschulus Tragicus); μηδέπω ' ν προοιμίοις only just beginning , (Aeschulus Tragicus); εἴ τι τοῦδε φρ. ματᾷ if any part of this presage be vain, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. generally, a hymn , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8906.definition:
reckless haste, vehemence, rashness, indiscretion , (Demosthenes Orator), etc. 
from προπετής (ML)

G8907.definition:
1. to fall or throw oneself forward , as in rowing, προπεσόντες ἔρεσσον, like Lat. incumbere remis, (Odyssey by Homer):—;of suppliants, to fall prostrate , (Euripides) 
2. to rush forward, rush headlong , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. to move forwards, advance before the rest, (Polybius Historicus): to project , (Polybius Historicus) 
4. προπίτνω poetry for προπίπτω 
5. to fall prostate , ἐς γᾶν (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8908.definition: in plural, like προπύλαια, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; in singular, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8909.definition: a going up, ascent , κλίμακος προσαμβάσεις ascent by means of ladders, i. e. scaling ladders, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πρ. (Euripides); τειχέων πρ. a place where they may be approached , (Euripides); δωμάτων πρ. i. e. the steps leading to the house, (Euripides) (ML)

G8911.definition:
1. to strike or dash against , τί τινι (Iliad by Homer); ἀψῖδα πέτρῳ πρ. letting it dash against , (Euripides); τὸν πρὶν ὄλβον ἕρματι πρ. to wreck his happiness on a rock, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πρ. θηρία τινί to set them on him, (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. δόρυ τινί (Euripides):—;without any notion of violence, to put to, apply , μαλακὰν χέρα πρ. [ ἕλκει] of a surgeon, (Pindar); πρ. παρειὰν παρηίδι (Euripides); ὄμματα τέκνοις (Euripides) 
2. to assign to, procure for , κέρδος τινί (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. Λακεδαιμονίοις Ὀλυμπιάδα to give them the honour of an Olympic victory, (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. κακὸν τῇ πόλει (Aeschulus Tragicus); εὔκλειαν σαυτῇ (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. δεῖμά τινι, Lat. incutere timorem alicui, (Euripides) 
3. with accusative of the object struck, ἀρούρας προσβάλλειν, of the Sun, to strike the earth with his rays, (Homer); of smells, βροτοῦ [ ὀσμὴ] με προσέβαλε (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. metaphorically to attend to a thing or to add , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
5. μή μ᾽ ἀνάγκῃ προσβάλῃς τάδ᾽ εἰκαθεῖν do not drive me by force to give way, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6. intransitive to strike against, to make an attack or assault upon , τινί (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; πρὸς τὸ τεῖχος (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute to attack, charge , (Herdotus Historicus); προσβαλὼν αἱρεῖ τὴν πόλιν by assault , (Xenophon Historicus) 
7. to put in with a ship, ἐς τὸν λιμένα (Thucydides); πρὸς Τάραντα (Thucydides); with dative, Σικελίᾳ (Thucydides) 
8. Mid. to throw oneself upon, attack , τινα (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8916.definition: to look at, behold , (Mimnermus Lyricus), etc.; compare aorist2 προσεῖδον:—;so in Mid., προσορωμένα (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8917.definition:
1. to speak to one, to address, accost , (Homer), etc.; πρ. ὀνόματί τινα (Demosthenes Orator):—;with double accusative, τί προσείπω ς᾽ ἔπο; (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to address as so and so, πρ. τινὰ ὡς ἀλλότριον (Plato Philosophus); πρ. τινὰ χαίρειν to bid him greeting , (Euripides) 
3. to call so and so, to name , τί νιν προσείπ; (Aeschulus Tragicus); τοῦτο γάρ ς᾽ ἔχω μόνον προσειπεῖν (Sophocles Tragicus); ὅν μοι προσεῖπας πόσιν whom thou didst name my husband, (Euripides) (ML)

G8920.definition: over and above, besides , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8922.definition:
1. soft, gentle, kindly , (Pindar); προσηνές τι λέγειν (Thucydides) 
2. with dative, λύχνῳ προσηνές, i. e. suitable for burning, (Herdotus Historicus) (For derivation, see. ἀπηνής). 
3. adverb -νῶς, (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G8924.definition:
1. a putting to, application of ladders to a wall, (Thucydides); of the cupping-glass, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. an adding, addition , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8926.definition: to set on fire or burn besides :—;Pass., σκεύη προσκεκαυμένα pots burnt at the fire , (Aristophanes Comicus): metaphorically, προσκαίεσθαί τινι to be in love with . . , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8927.definition:
1. to leave besides as a legacy , ἀρχήν τινι (Thucydides) 
2. to lose besides , τὰ αὑτῶν (Thucydides) (ML)

G8929.definition:
1. to be placed or laid by or upon, to lie by or upon , οὔατα προσέκειτο handles were upon it, (Iliad by Homer); τῇ θύρᾳ προσκεῖσθαι to keep close to the door, (Aristophanes Comicus); δοκοὶ τῷ τείχει προσκείμεναι lying near the wall, (Thucydides):—; ὁ προσκείμενος ἵππος the inside horse (turning a corner), (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. to lie beside, cling to , (Sophocles Tragicus): of a woman, to be given to wife , τινί (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. generally, to be involved in or bound up with good or evil, with dative, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. to be attached or devoted to , τινί (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; πρ. τῷ λεγομένῳ to put faith in a story, (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. οἴνῳ to be addicted to wine, (Herdotus Historicus); ἄγραις hunting, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 
5. to press upon, be urgent with a person, with dative, (Herdotus Historicus); προσκείμενος with zeal , (Thucydides) 
6. in military sense, to press close or hard, pursue closely , τινί (Thucydides); absolute to follow close , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ προσκείμενον the enemy , (Herdotus Historicus) 
7. with a thing for the subject, to fall to, belong to , τοῖσι θεῶν τιμὴ αὕτη προσκέαται (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. τινι δοῦλος (Euripides):—; to be laid upon as a charge, to do something, with infinitive, (Herdotus Historicus) 
8. to be added or attached to , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;absolute, ἡ χάρις προσκείσεται (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8931.definition:
1. to strike against , τινί (Plato Philosophus):absolute to stumble, fail , (Plutarch) 
2. to have a collision with another, give offence , (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. τινί (Plutarch) 
3. to take offence at, be angry with , τινί (Demosthenes Orator), etc.: —;absolute to take offence , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8932.definition:
1. Dep.: 
2. to reckon or count in addition to , τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. to impute , τί τινι (Plutarch) (ML)

G8935.definition:
1. a going or coming to, an approach , ἡ πρ. μάλιστα ταύτῃ ἐγένετο the approach was most feasible on this part, (Herdotus Historicus); ἀπείπατο τὴν πρ. rejected his advances , (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. μελάθρων approach to the halls, (Euripides) 
2. an onset , πρόσοδοι τῆς μάχης onsets or attacks , (Euripides) 
3. like πομπή II, a solemn procession to a temple with singing and music, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. the coming forward of a speaker in a public assembly , γράφεσθαι πρόσοδον to petition for a hearing , (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. ποιεῖσθαι πρὸς τὸν δῆμον (Aeschines Orator) 
5. income, rent , as opposite to principal, (Demosthenes Orator); often in plural, (Isaeus Orator) 
6. of the public revenue, φόρων πρόσοδος (Herdotus Historicus); χρημάτων πρ. (Thucydides); mostly in plural the returns, revenue , Lat. reditus, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8936.definition: intransitive to smell of, be redolent of , with genitive, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8939.definition:
1. appearance, aspect, mien , (Pindar); periphrastic, σὴ πρ. thy presence , i. e. thyself , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. a seeing, beholding, sight, view , (Euripides) (ML)

G8940.definition:
1. to play or sport with , τινί (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. absolute to sport, jest , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. with accusative, πρ. θεούς to sing to the gods, ὕμνον πρ. τὸν Ἔρωτα sang a hymn in praise of Eros, (Plato Philosophus) 
4. to banter , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8941.definition: to sprinkle on one, τινί τι (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G8943.definition: an ordinance, command , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; ἐκ προστάγματος (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8945.definition:
1. one who stands before, a front-rank-man , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. a chief, leader of a party, (Herdotus Historicus); ὁ πρ. τοῦ δήμου (Thucydides) 
3. generally, a president, ruler , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; προστάται τῆς εἰρήνης its chief authors , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. one who stands before, a protector, guard, champion , πυλωμάτων (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
5. at Athens, of a citizen who took care of the μέτοικοι, as the Rom. patronus took care of his clientes; προστάτην γράφεσθαί τινα to choose as one's patron , (Aristophanes Comicus); but, γράφεσθαι προστάτου to enter oneself by one's patron's name , attach oneself to a patron , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6. προστάτης θεοῦ one who stands before a god to entreat him, a suppliant , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8948.definition:
a deposit made by water , πρ. Νείλου, of the Delta of the Nile, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
from προσχώννυ_μι (ML)

G8949.definition:
1. to go to, approach , with dative, (Herdotus Historicus); absolute, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. to come or go over to, come in, join , τινί or πρός τινα (Herdotus Historicus), attic; absolute, (Thucydides); also, πρ. ἐς ὁμολογίαν or ὁμολογίᾳ (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. to accede to an opinion, (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. λόγοις τινός (Sophocles Tragicus): to make concessions , (Euripides) 
4. to approach , i. e. to agree with, be like , τινί or πρός τινα (Herdotus Historicus) 
5. to put faith in, believe , τινί (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8952.definition:
1. the foremost or upper part of anything: a bust or half-figure , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. the forepart of a ship, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8953.definition:
1. Dep.: 
2. to set up as a pretext or excuse, allege by way of excuse, plead in excuse , with accusative, (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; with infinitive to allege as an excuse that . . , (Demosthenes Orator):—;absolute to make excuses , (Thucydides):—;aor1 προφασισθῆναι in passive sense, to be used as a pretext , (Thucydides) 
3. to allege (by way of accusation) that , (Plato Philosophus) 
from πρόφᾶσις (ML)

G8955.definition: a guard in front; in plural outposts, videttes, piquets , (Xenophon Historicus); in singular, ἡ πρ. αὐτοῦ his advanced guard, (Xenophon Historicus); διὰ προφυλακῆς with an advanced guard , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8956.definition:
an advanced guard : οἱ προφύλακες 
= αἱ προφυλακαί, (Thucydides) (ML)

G8957.definition: to keep guard before, to guard a place or house, with accusative, (Homeric Hymns) (in the epic 2nd plural imperative προφύλαχθε, for προφυλάσσετε); (Xenophon Historicus); προφυλάσσειν ἐπί τινι to keep guard over a person or place, (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute to be on guard, keep watch , ἡ προφυλάσσουσα (i.e. ναῦς); = προφυλακίς, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Mid. to guard oneself, to be on one's guard, take precautions , (Herdotus Historicus):—;with accusative to be on one's guard or take precautions against , Lat. cavere, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8958.definition:
1. at hand, ready , (Aeschulus Tragicus); of a drawn sword or knife, (Sophocles Tragicus); λίθοις καὶ . . ἀκοντίοις, ὡς ἕκαστός τι πρόχειρον εἶχε (Thucydides); ὃ προχειρότατον ἔχω εἰπεῖν (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. πρόχειρόν [ ἐστι] it is easy , with infinitive, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
3. of persons, ready to do, with infinitive, (Sophocles Tragicus); with dative, πρ. τῇ φυγῇ ready for flight, (Euripides) 
4. adverb -ρως, off-hand, readily , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8960.definition:
1. lately, just now , Lat. nuper, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. the day before yesterday , οὐ χθές, ἀλλὰ πρ. (Thucydides); πρώην τε καὶ χθές till yesterday or the day before , i. e. till very lately , (Herdotus Historicus); so, χθές τε καὶ πρώην (Aristophanes Comicus); πρώην καὶ χθές (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8962.definition:
the officer in command at the bow, the look-out man , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
(ML)

G8967.definition:
1. first-born, firstling , (Iliad by Homer); φοῖνιξ πρ. first-created , (Euripides) 
2. of rank, πρ. οἶκοι high-born houses, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. first-ordained , (Lucian) (ML)

G8969.gloss: to give a right of first-born
G8969.definition: to give a right of first-born

G8973.definition: to stomp; catch by a heel

G8975.definition:
1. mostly in plural feathers , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; in singular a feather , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. = πτέρυξ, a bird's wing , in plural wings , (Homer); Παλλάδος ὑπὸ πτεροῖς ὄντας, metaphorically from chickens under the hen's wings, (Aeschulus Tragicus): —; τῷ πτερὰ γίγνετο he got as it were wings , i. e. spirit, courage, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. the wings of a bat (see. πτίλον II), (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. any winged creature , as the Sphinx, (Euripides); a beetle, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
5. like οἰωνός, Lat. avis, an augury, omen, (Pindar) 
6. anything like wings : as 
7. a ship's wings , i. e. oars (compare πτερόω); ἐρετμά, τά τε πτερὰ νηυσὶ πέλονται (Odyssey by Homer); νηὸς πτερά (Hesiod):—; hence birds are said πτεροῖς ἐρέσσειν, (Euripides) 
8. ἀέθλων πτερά, i. e. the wings of victory, which lift the Poet to heaven, (Pindar) 
9. a feathered arrow , (Euripides) 
10. τοῦ πώγωνος τὰ πτερά the points of the beard, (Lucian) 
11. in Architecture, of the rows of columns along the sides of Greek temples, see. ἄπτερος. (ML)

G8977.definition: attic -ττομαι, future ξομαι, Dep. to clap the wings like a cock crowing, (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

G8978.definition:
1. feathered , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. winged , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. πτερωτοί (i.e. ὄρνιθες); feathered fowl, birds , (Euripides) (ML)

G8979.definition:
1. to frighten, scare, alarm , Lat. terrere, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. intransitive to crouch or cower down for fear (compare πτώσσω), properly of animals, (Sophocles Tragicus); of men, (Pindar), attic; πτ. βωμὸν ὕπο (Euripides); also with accusative loci, πτ. βωμόν to flee cowering to the altar, (Euripides) 
3. to crouch like a wild beast ready to spring, (Euripides);—;so of men in ambush, ὑπὸ τεύχεσι πεπτηῶτες (Odyssey by Homer) 
4. with accusative rei, to crouch for fear of , ἀπειλάς (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8985.definition:
1. white-rump , the name of a kind of antelope, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. the white-tailed eagle, the erne , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. (ML)

G8986.definition:
1. the hollow bottom or stand of a cup , Lat. fundus, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. of the sea, the bottom, depth , (Hesiod), etc. 
3. the bottom or foundation of a thing, in plural, χθόνα ἐκ πυθμένων κραδαίνειν (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐκ π. ἔκλινε κλῇθρα (Sophocles Tragicus); δίκας π. the anvil-stand on which is forged the sword of retribution, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. the bottom, stock, root of a tree , (Odyssey by Homer):—;metaphorically the stem or stock of a family, (Aeschulus Tragicus); σμικροῦ γένοιτ᾽ ἂν σπέρματος π. μέγας, i. e. great things might come from small, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
(ML)

G8987.definition:
1. to make close, cover or wrap up, enwrap , (Iliad by Homer); π. νῆα λίθοισι to surround a ship with stones, so as to protect it when laid up, (Hesiod):—; to cover thickly , of a youth's chin, (Odyssey by Homer); πυκ. στεφάνοις to cover thick with crowns, (Euripides); so in Mid., στεφάνοις κεφαλὰς πυκασώμεθα [variant datesAnthology Palantina; also without στεφάνοις, to crown, deck with garlands , (Euripides):—;Pass., στέμμασι πυκασθείς (Herdotus Historicus); δάφνῃ πυκασθείς (Euripides); perfect participle πεπυκασμένος, thickly covered , ὄρος πεπυκασμένον a hill well-clothed with wood, (Hesiod):—;Mid., πυκάζου cover thyself , (Euripides) 
2. metaphorically, Ἕκτορα ἄχος πύκασε φρένας threw a shadow over his heart, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., νόον πεπυκασμένος, close, cautious of mind, (Hesiod) 
3. to close, shut, shut up , ἐντὸς πυκάζειν σφέας αὐτούς to shut themselves close up within, (Odyssey by Homer); πύκαζε (i.e. τὸ δῶμα); shut it close , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8988.definition: a gate-keeper, warder, porter (see. πυλαωρός); (Aeschulus Tragicus); also as feminine, ἡ π. δωμάτων γυνή (Euripides):—;metaphorically, τοῖον πυλωρὸν φύλακα τροφῆς such a watchful guardian of thy life, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8989.definition:
a tablet of box-wood , (Lucian) 
from πυξίς (ML)

G8992.definition: mostly in plural pieces of wood , rubbed one against another to produce fire, (Homeric Hymns), etc. (ML)

G8993.definition: or -καυτος, burnt in fire , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8994.definition: wheat , (Homer); also in plural, (Odyssey by Homer), etc. (ML)

G8998.definition:
1. to light up, kindle , πυρσεύσας σέλας Εὐβοίαν having lit up Euboea with beacon-fires σέλας combining with the notion of the Verb), (Euripides) 
2. to make signals by torches or beacon-fires , (Xenophon Historicus): metaphorically, πυρσεύετε κραυγὴν ἀγῶνος give a shout in signal of battle, (Euripides):—;Pass., δόξα ὥσπερ ἀπὸ σκοπῆς πυρσεύεται (Plutarch): impersonal, πυρσεύεται fire-signals are made , (Lucian) (ML)

G8999.definition:
1. a firebrand, torch , (Iliad by Homer):—;in plural fires , [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;metaphorically, πυρσὸς ὕμνων (Pindar); plural the fires of love , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
2. a beacon or signal-fire, bale-fire , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. plural πύρσα, watch-fires , (Euripides) (ML)

G9000.definition:
1. fire-bearing , (Aeschulus Tragicus); of lightning, (Pindar):—; πυρφόροι ὀϊστοί arrows with combustibles tied to them , (Thucydides) 
2. in special senses, 
3. epithet of Zeus in reference to his lightnings, (Sophocles Tragicus); of Demeter, in reference to the torches used by her worshippers, (Euripides); of Artemis, (Sophocles Tragicus); but θεὸς πυρφόρος the fire-bearing god, the god who produces plague or fever , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. ὁ πυρφόρος, in the Lacedaemonian army, was the priest who kept the sacrificial fire , which was never allowed to go out, (Xenophon Historicus); hence proverbial of a total defeat, ἔδεε δὲ μηδὲ πυρφόρον περιγενέσθαι (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9002.definition: the beard , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;metaphorically, πώγων πυρός a beard or tail of fire, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9006.definition: to leave off work, to be remiss , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9007.definition:
1. to sprinkle, besprinkle , ῥάσσατε (i.e. δῶμα ὕδατι) (Odyssey by Homer); αἵματι βωμόν (Euripides):—;Pass., πύργοι αἵματι ἐρράδατ᾽ (Iliad by Homer); αἵματι δ᾽ ἐρράδαται τοῖχοι (Odyssey by Homer):—;of dust, ἵπποι ῥαίνοντο κονίηι (Iliad by Homer) 
2. metaphorically, ῥ. τινὰ ὕμνωι (Pindar) 
3. to sprinkle , with accusative of the thing sprinkled, ῥαίνειν ἐς τὰ βλέφαρα to sprinkle (vinegar) in their eyes, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9012.definition:
1. stitched, patched , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. metaphorically strung together, continuous , of verses, (Pindar) 
3. worked with the needle : ῥαπτόν, οῦ, an embroidered carpet , (Xenophon Historicus); ῥαπτὴ σφαῖρα a stitched ball, of divers colours, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
(ML)

G9013.definition:
1. to sew or stitch together, stich , (Iliad by Homer):—; Mid., ῥάπτεσθαι ὀχετὸν δερμάτων to make oneself a pipe of leather, (Herdotus Historicus); ῥαψάμενος τουτί (i.e. τὸ προσκεφάλαιον) having got it stitched , (Aristophanes Comicus); but also, to sew on or to one , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass., ἐρράφθαι τὸ χεῖλος to have one's lip sewed up , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. metaphorically to devise, contrive, plot , (Homer), etc.; proverbial, τὸ ὑπόδημα ἔρραψας μὲν σύ, ὑπεδήσατο δὲ Ἀρισταγόρης you made the shoe , but Aristagoras put it on, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9018.definition:
1. the lower part of the back, the chine , (Iliad by Homer): then, the spine or backbone , ὑπὸ ῥάχιν παγῆναι to be impaled, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. anything ridged like the backbone, a mountain-ridge , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9022.definition:
1. a saying, speaking, speech , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; ἡ ἀπὸ Σκυθῶν ῥῆσις the Scythian phrase , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. a resolution, declaration , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. a tale, legend , (Pindar) 
4. a phrase or passage, a speech in a play , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9024.definition:
1. stated, specified , (Iliad by Homer); ἐς χρόνον ῥητόν at a set or stated time, (Herdotus Historicus); ἡμέραι ῥ. (Thucydides); ἐπὶ ῥητοῖς γέρασι with fixed prerogatives, (Thucydides); ῥ. ἀργύριον a stated sum, (Thucydides); ἐπὶ ῥητοῖς on stated terms, on certain conditions , (Herdotus Historicus):—;adverb ῥητῶς, expressly, distinctly , (New Testament) 
2. spoken of, known, famous , (Hesiod) 
3. that may be spoken or told , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ῥητὸν ἄρρητόν τ᾽ ἔπος, Lat. fas nefasque, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. in Mathem., ῥητά are rational quantities , opposite to surds ἄλογα); (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9025.definition:
frost, cold , Lat. frigus, (Odyssey by Homer), etc. 
(ML)

G9026.definition: a root : metaphorically a stem, race (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9029.definition:
1. ionic and epic ῥοιή, a pomegranate-tree , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. the fruit, a pomegranate , (Homeric Hymns) 
3. a knob shaped like a pomegranate , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9030.definition: to whistle , Lat. stridere, (Iliad by Homer); of a snake, to hiss , (Hesiod):—;Pass. to rush through the air , ἐρροίζητο (3rd singular pluperfect) [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9031.definition:
1. the whistling or whizzing of an arrow, (Iliad by Homer):—;any whistling or piping sound , as of a shepherd, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. rushing motion, a rush, swing , (Plutarch) 
Formed from the sound. (ML)

G9033.definition:
1. a club, cudgel , thicker at the buttend; used to cudgel an ass, (Iliad by Homer); to walk with, (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; a war-club or mace , shod with metal, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. = ῥόπτρον III, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9034.definition:
ῥοπή, -ῆς, ἡ 
(ῥέπω, to incline) [in LXX: Isa.40:15 (שַׁחַק), etc. ;] 
inclination downwards, as the turn of the scale: L, mg., for ῥιπή, which see, 1Co.15:52 (see Tdf., in l).†
(AS)

G9036.definition: a rushing stream, a torrent , (Thucydides); ὁ ῥ. τοῦ πυρός, of a stream of lava , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9037.definition: to bring into measure or proportion : generally, to order, to educate, train , (Xenophon Historicus), etc.:—;metaphorically, ῥ. λύπην ὅπου to define the place of grief, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Mid., ῥ. πλόκαμον to arrange one's hair, (Euripides):—;Pass., νηλεῶς ὧδ᾽ ἐρρύθμισμαι thus ruthlessly am I brought to order , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9038.definition:
1. measured motion, time, rhythm , Lat. numerus, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: —; ἐν ῥυθμῷ in time , Virgil 's in numerum , (Xenophon Historicus); μετὰ ῥυθμοῦ (Thucydides); θάττονα ῥυθμὸν ἐπάγειν to play in quicker time , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. proportion or symmetry of parts, (Plato Philosophus) 
3. generally, arrangement, order , (Euripides) 
4. the state or condition of the soul, temper, disposition , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc. 
5. the form or shape of a thing, (Herdotus Historicus); of a breastplate, (Xenophon Historicus) 
6. the wise, manner or fashion of a thing, (Euripides); τίς ῥ. φόνο; what kind of slaughter? (Euripides) (ML)

G9043.definition: to keep the Sabbath , (Septuagint Greek Bible) (ML)

G9046.definition:
1. mostly in plural covering: the covering of a shield , (Euripides): a large cloak , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. a pack-saddle , (Strabo Geographus) 
3. a pile , ὅπλων (Plutarch) (ML)

G9050.definition:
1. rotten, decayed, unsound, cracked , (Plato Philosophus)—;adverb, σαθρῶς ἱδρυμένος built on unsound foundations, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. metaphorically, πρίν τι καὶ σαθρὸν ἐγγίνεσθαί σφι before any unsound thought comes into their heads, i. e. before they prove traitors, (Herdotus Historicus); ς. λόγοι (Euripides) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G9052.definition:
1. a triangular musical instrument with four strings , Lat. sambuca, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. an engine of like form used in sieges, (Plutarch) (ML)

G9058.definition: a satrapy, the office or province of a satrap , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9059.definition:
a satrap, viceroy , Lat. satrapa, (Xenophon Historicus) 
Persian word. (ML)

G9063.definition:
1. a Siren : in plural Σειρῆνες, αἱ, the Sirens , mythical sisters on the south coast of Italy, who enticed seamen by their songs, and then slew them, (Odyssey by Homer) (Homer) only knows of two , whence epic dual. genitive Σειρήνοιιν. 
2. metaphorically a Siren, deceitful woman , (Euripides): the Siren charm of eloquence, (Aeschines Orator) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G9065.definition: a plank : metaphorically a leaf of papyrus: —; generally, the page of a book , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9069.definition:
a standard , (Polybius Historicus):—; a band under one standard , the Roman manipulus , (Polybius Historicus) 
(ML)

G9073.definition:
1. strength, might , (Iliad by Homer):—;with infinitive, σθ. πολεμίζειν strength to war, (Iliad by Homer); σθ. ὥστε καθελεῖν (Euripides); σθένει by force , (Sophocles Tragicus); λόγῳ τε καὶ σθένει both by right and might , (Sophocles Tragicus); so, ὑπὸ σθένους (Euripides); παντὶ σθένει with all one's might , (Thucydides) 
2. strength, might , of all kinds moral as well as physical, σθένος τῆς ἀληθείας (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀγγέλων σθ. their might or authority , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. a force of men, like δύναμις, (Iliad by Homer) 
4. metaphorically, like Lat. vis for copia, a quantity, profusion , (Pindar) 
5. periphrastic, like βίη, ἴς, μένος, as σθένος Ἰδομενῆος, Ὠρίωνος, for Idomeneus, Orion, themselves, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G9075.definition:
1. silently , σῖγα ἔχειν to be silent , (Sophocles Tragicus); κάθησο σῖγα (Aristophanes Comicus); alone, σῖγα hush! be still! (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;the public crier proclaiming silence said σῖγα πᾶς (i.e. ἔστω); (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. under one's breath, in a whisper, secretly , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9076.definition: an implement or tool of iron , σιδηρίων ἐπαί̈ειν to feel iron , not to be proof against it, (Herdotus Historicus); θερμὰ σιδήρια hot irons , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9086.definition: want of corn or food , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9089.definition:
1. ς. ἀνάγκη the task of grinding and baking , (Euripides) 
2. as Substantive one that ground the corn in the handmill , (Thucydides); mostly feminine a baking-woman , (Herdotus Historicus); γυναῖκες ς. (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9090.definition:
1. silence , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; σιωπὴν ποιεῖν (Xenophon Historicus); ἦν ς. there was a hush or calm , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. the habit of silence , (Demosthenes Orator) 
3. dative σιωπῇ as adverb, in silence , (Homer), attic 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G9096.definition:
a carpenter's axe or adze , used for smoothing the trunks of trees, different from the πέλεκυς, (Odyssey by Homer) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G9098.definition: a covering, shelter, protection , (Xenophon Historicus):—;with genitive, ἐν σκέπῃ τοῦ πολέμου under shelter from war, (Herdotus Historicus); ὑπὸ τὴν Ῥωμαίων σκέπην under their protection , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9100.definition:
1. to look about, look carefully , followed by preposition εἰς, (Odyssey by Homer):—;with accusative to look after, watch , (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;absolute to look out, reconnoitre , (Herdotus Historicus); σκέψαι look , (Aeschulus Tragicus); σκέψασθε look out , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. of the mind, to look to, view, examine, consider, think on , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.:—; σκέψασθε δέ: only consider , (Thucydides) 
3. to think of beforehand, premeditate , (Demosthenes Orator) 
4. perfect also in passive sense, ἐσκεμμένα things well-considered , (Thucydides); σκοπεῖτε οὖν. Answ. ἔσκεπται (Plato Philosophus); so 3 future passive ἐσκέψεται (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9104.definition:
1. a staff or stick to lean upon, a walking-stick , (Homer): metaphorically of the daughters of Oedipus, σκῆπτρα φωτός his staffs or supports , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. a staff , as the badge of command, a sceptre : in (Homer) borne by chiefs, and transmitted from father to son, whence the passage in (Iliad by Homer) 2 is called ἡ τοῦ σκήπτρου παράδοσις, (Thucydides):—;also borne by judges, by heralds, by speakers, who on rising to speak received it from the herald, (Homer) 
3. the sceptre , i. e. royalty, kingly power, rule , [8th/7th c.BC, variant datesTragica Adespota (ML)

G9106.definition:
1. to overshadow, shade , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. generally, to overshadow, cover , (Hesiod):—;Pass., (Euripides) 
3. to shade in painting , (Lucian) (ML)

G9112.definition: crookedness , (Plutarch): in plural the windings of a stream, etc., (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G9115.definition:
1. a lookout-place, a mountain-peak , (Homer): of the Trojan acropolis, (Euripides): compare σκόπελος. 
2. metaphorically the height or highest point of anything, (Pindar) 
3. a watchtower , Lat. specula, (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. a look-out, watch , σκοπιὴν ἔχειν to keep watch , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G9119.definition:
to look angry or sullen, be of a sad countenance , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
from σκυθρωπός (ML)

G9120.definition:
1. to strip or despoil a slain enemy of his arms, (Hesiod); with accusative of persons or things, Κύκνον σκυλεύσαντες ἀπp ὤμων τεύχεα having stript the arms of Cycnus from his shoulders, (Hesiod) 
2. with accusative rei et genitive pers. to strip the arms off an enemy, (Xenophon Historicus); so, ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν σκ. ψέλια (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9121.definition: a cub, whelp , especially a lion's whelp , (Iliad by Homer), attic; of other animals, (Euripides); in poets also of men, Ἀχίλλειος σκ. (Euripides) (ML)

G9122.definition:
1. a staff, cudgel, club , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. at Sparta, a staff or baton , used as a cypher for writing dispatches:—;a strip of leather was rolled slantwise round it, on which the dispatches were written lengthwise, so that when unrolled they were unintelligible: commanders abroad had a staff of like thickness, round which they rolled these papers, and so were able to read the dispatches:—;hence σκυτάλη came to mean a Spartan dispatch , (Thucydides); and generally a message , (Pindar) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G9127.definition:
1. Lat. taxus, the yew, (Plato Philosophus) 
2. the convolvulus , or perhaps bryony , [variant datesTragica Adespota, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9130.definition:
1. a master of one's craft or art, an adept , of a diviner, (Herdotus Historicus); of poets, (Pindar); of the Creator, (Plato Philosophus); metaphorically, ς. πημάτων an adept in misery, (Euripides) 
2. like φρόνιμος, one who is clever in matters of life, a wise man , in which sense the seven Sages are called σοφισταί, (Herdotus Historicus); of Prometheus, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. at Athens, a Sophist , i. e. a professor of grammar, rhetoric, politics, mathematics, such as Prodicus, Gorgias, Protagoras, (Thucydides), etc. At first the Sophists were held in honour; but from their loose principles they fell into ill repute, and the word came to mean, 
4. a sophist (in bad sense), a quibbler, cheat , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

G9134.definition:
1. of things, to be rare, scarce, scanty , (Pindar) 
2. of persons, to lack or be in want of , τινός (Herdotus Historicus), etc.;—;so in Pass., ἐσπανίσμεθ᾽ ἀρωγῶν (Aeschulus Tragicus): absolute to be in want , (Euripides) (ML)

G9135.definition:
1. rare, scarce, scanty , (Herdotus Historicus); σπάνιον ἑαυτὸν παρέχειν, Lat. difficiles aditus habere, (Plato Philosophus); ὕδατι σπανίῳ χρώμενοι having a scanty supply of water, (Thucydides); with infinitive, σπ. ἰδεῖν rare to behold, (Xenophon Historicus): of persons in an adverb sense, σπάνιος ἐπιφοιτᾷ he seldom visits, (Herdotus Historicus):—; σπάνιόν ἐστι, with infinitive, it is seldom that . ., (Xenophon Historicus):—; τὸ σπάνιον = σπάνις, (Aeschines Orator) 
2. comparative σπανιώτερος, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Sup. -ώτατος, attic 
3. adverb -ίως, seldom , (Xenophon Historicus); so σπανίᾳ, (Plato Philosophus): comparative -ιώτερον, (Thucydides) (ML)

G9136.definition: a swathing band , and in plural swaddling-clothes , (Homeric Hymns); παῖς ἔτ᾽ ὢν ἐν σπαργάνοις (Aeschulus Tragicus); tokens by which a person is identified , Lat. monumenta, crepundia, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9140.definition:
the space one can span with the thumb and little finger, a span , Lat. dodrans, about 7 1/2 inches , (Herdotus Historicus) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G9141.definition: a spark , Lat. scintilla, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G9142.definition:
1. a heap of ashes, ashes , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. metaphorically, = σποδός III, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9145.definition:
1. a drink-offering , i. e. the wine poured out to the gods before drinking, Lat. libatio, (Hesiod); σπονδὰς θεοῖς λείβειν, σπένδειν (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. in plural, σπονδαί was a solemn treaty or truce , (because solemn drink-offerings were made on concluding them); σπονδαὶ ἄκρητοι the truce made by pouring unmixed wine, (Iliad by Homer); αἱ Λακεδαιμονίων σπ. the truce with them. (Thucydides); σπονδὰς παραδιδόναι (Aristophanes Comicus); δέχεσθαι (Thucydides); τυχεῖν (Xenophon Historicus); σπ. ποιεῖσθαί τινι to make a truce with one, (Herdotus Historicus); πρός τινα (Aristophanes Comicus); σπ. τέμνειν (like ὅρκια τέμνειν); (Euripides); σπ. ἄγειν πρός τινας (Thucydides) 
3. αἱ Ὀλυμπικαὶ σπ. the solemn truce or armistice during the Olympic games, (Thucydides) 
4. the treaty itself , εἴρηται ἐν ταῖς σπ. (Thucydides) (ML)

G9147.definition:
1. of persons, 
2. with accusative rei, to drop, let fall or shed drop by drop , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
3. with dative rei, αἵματι στ. to drip with blood, (Aeschulus Tragicus); στάζων ἱδρῶτι (Sophocles Tragicus);—;rarely with genitive, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
4. intransitive of things, to drop, fall in drops, drip, trickle , (Herdotus Historicus); metaphorically, στάζει ἐν ὕπνωι πόνος (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9148.definition:
1. to measure by rule , (Euripides): —;Pass., with future middle -ήσομαι, to be measured, estimated , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. as Dep. (see. σταθμόω); to estimate distance or size, without actual measurement, (Herdotus Historicus): metaphorically to estimate one thing by another, τί τινι (Plato Philosophus); absolute to conjecture , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. to attach weight to a thing, value it, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9150.definition:
1. a standing place for animals, Lat. stabulum, a stable, fold, (Iliad by Homer): a stye , (Odyssey by Homer): of men, a dwelling, abode , (Hesiod) 
2. quarters, lodgings for travellers or soldiers, Lat. statio, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. in Persia, σταθμοί were stations on the royal road, where the king rested, (Herdotus Historicus): hence a day's journey, day's march , averaging about 5 parasangs or 15 miles, (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. like Lat. statio, a station for ships, (Euripides) 
5. an upright post, the bearing pillar of the roof, (Odyssey by Homer): a door-post , especially in plural, (Homer), attic 
6. the balance , (Aristophanes Comicus); ἱστᾶν σταθμῷ τι πρός τι to weigh one thing against another, (Herdotus Historicus) 
7. weight , σταθμὸν ἔχειν τάλαντον to weigh a talent, (Herdotus Historicus); absolute in accusative, ἴσα σταθμόν equal in weight , (Herdotus Historicus); ἡμιπλίνθια σταθμὸν διτάλαντα two talents in or by weight , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural weights , (Euripides), etc. (ML)

G9151.definition: flour of spelt mixed and made into dough , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9155.definition: stiff fat, tallow, suet , Lat. sebum, opp. toπιμελή (Lat. adeps, soft fat), (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G9157.definition: to cover , (Xenophon Historicus): metaphorically, ὕπνος στ. τινά covers, embraces one, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., πλοῖον ἐστεγασμένον a decked vessel, (Antipho Orator) (ML)

G9158.definition:
1. waterproof , (Herdotus Historicus); στεγνὰ οἰκήματα, of a cave, (Euripides) 
2. as Substantive, στεγνόν, οῦ, a covered dwelling , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9159.definition: the crown of the root, stump , whence the trunk springs, Lat. codex, (Pindar) (ML)

G9160.definition: a mass of olives from which the oil has been pressed, olive-cake , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9161.definition:
1. to be mourned, giving cause for grief , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. mournful , (Euripides) 
(ML)

G9162.definition:
1. to moan, sigh, groan , (Homer) 
2. with genitive to moan or sigh for , (Euripides); ὑπέρ τινος (Aeschulus Tragicus); τινί or ἐπί τινι (Euripides); with accusative cognate, πένθος οἰκεῖον στ. (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Mid., (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. with accusative to bewail, lament , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; στένειν τινὰ τῆς τύχης to pity him for his ill fortune, (Aeschulus Tragicus): so in Mid., στένεσθαί τινα (Euripides) (ML)

G9166.definition:
1. to deprive, bereave, rob of anything, with accusative pers. et genitive rei, (Odyssey by Homer), attic 
2. with accusative rei, to take away , [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Pass. to have taken from one , βίον στερείς (Euripides) (ML)

G9167.definition: to deprive of a thing, (Thucydides):—;Pass. to be deprived of a thing, (Herdotus Historicus), attic (ML)

G9168.definition:
1. anything that encircles the head, for defence or ornament: 
2. the brim of the helmet, projecting behind as well as before, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. part of a woman's head-dress, a diadem, coronal , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;metaphorically, of a city, ἀπὸ στεφάναν κέκαρσαι πύργων thou hast been shorn of thy coronal of towers, (Euripides) 
4. the brim or edge of anything, the brow of a hill, edge of a cliff , (Iliad by Homer); of a basket, (Moschus Bucolicus) (ML)

G9171.definition:
1. a block of stone used as a prop or buttress to a wall , (Iliad by Homer): a block of rockcrystal, in which the Egyptian mummies were cased, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. a block or slab , bearing an inscription; and so, 
3. a gravestone , (Homer), attic 
4. a block or slab , inscribed with record of victories, dedications, treaties, decrees, etc., (Herdotus Historicus), attic; γράφειν τινὰ εἰς στήλην, ἀναγράφειν ἐν στήλῃ, whether for honour, or for infamy, (Herdotus Historicus):—;also the record itself, a contract, agreement , κατὰ τὴν στήλην according to agreement , (Aristophanes Comicus); στῆλαι αἱ πρὸς Θηβαίους (Demosthenes Orator) 
5. a boundary post, (Xenophon Historicus):—; the turning-post at the end of the racecourse, Lat. meta, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6. for Στῆλαι Ἡρακλήιαι, see. Ἡράκλειος. (ML)

G9173.definition: to set up as a monument , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9175.definition:
1. the warp in the ancient upright loom, (Hesiod) 
2. a thread , (Batrachomyomachia) (ML)

G9180.definition: Mid. or Pass. to paint one's eyelids and eyebrows with black paint στίβι); (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G9181.definition: punctured , [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;generally, spotted, dappled , (Sophocles Tragicus); στικτὰ ὄμματα, of the hundred eyes of Argus, (Euripides) (ML)

G9184.definition:
1. a row or file of soldiers, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. a line of poetry, a verse , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9186.definition: a plant used for stuffing or padding; and metaphorically " padding , " an expletive , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9187.definition:
1. to set a row of poles with nets to drive the game into, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. to order or arrange in system , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9188.definition:
1. to put in trim , στολίσας νηὸς πτερά having trimmed the sails, (Hesiod) 
2. to equip, dress :—;Pass., ἐστολισμένος δορί armed with spear, (Euripides) 
3. metaphorically to deck, adorn , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9191.definition:
1. to aim or shoot at , with genitive, τοῦ σκοποῦ (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2. metaphorically to aim at, endeavour after , (Plato Philosophus); στ. φίλων κριτῶν to aim at having friends as judges, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. to endeavour to make out, to guess at a thing, with genitive, (Isocrates Orator):—; absolute to make guesses, conjecture, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9198.definition:
1. to encamp, bivouac, take up a position , (Xenophon Historicus): 
2. as Dep. στρατοπεδεύομαι, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; perfect ἐστρατοπεδεῦσθαι to be in camp , (Xenophon Historicus): of a fleet, to be stationed , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9199.definition: twisted, crooked , (Aristotle Philosopher); of the brows, knit, wrinkled , [variant datesAnthology Palantina: metaphorically, στρεβλοῖσι παλαίσμασι by cunning dodges in wrestling, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9202.definition: to twist, twirl or whirl about , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;metaphorically to make dizzy, distract , (Aeschulus Tragicus): —;Pass. to whirl about , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9203.definition:
1. round, spherical , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; λίθοι στρ. pebbles , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. circular , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. round, compactly formed , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. of ships, στρ. ναῦς, στρ. πλοῖον, a merchant- ship, from its round shape , as opposite to the long narrow ship-of-war μακρὰ ναῦς); (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
5. metaphorically of phrases, well-rounded, compact, pithy, terse , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;adverb, στρογγυλώτατα as tersely as possible , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G9207.definition:
1. the sparrow , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. ὁ μέγας στρ. the large bird , i. e. the ostrich, Struthio , (Xenophon Historicus): also called στρουθὸς κατάγαιος (i. e. the bird that runs on the ground , does not fly), (Herdotus Historicus); also simply στρουθός, like στρουθοκάμηλος, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9208.definition: the socket in which the pivot of a door ὁ στρόφιγξ); moved, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9209.definition:
1. a turning , e.g. of a horse, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν στροφαῖσιν ὀμμάτων with rolling of the eyes, (Euripides) 
2. a twist , such as wrestlers make to elude their adversary, (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically a trick, dodge , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. the turning of the Chorus as they danced from right to left of the ὀρχήστρα: the strain sung during this evolution, the strophe , to which the ἀντιστροφή answers. (ML)

G9210.definition:
1. the pivot, axle or pin on which a body turns , (Euripides) 
2. στρόφιγγες were pivots working in sockets , at top and bottom of a door, which served instead of hinges, (Plutarch) 
3. metaphorically, στρ. γλώττης, of a well-hung tongue, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9212.definition:
1. anything spread or laid out for lying or sitting upon, a mattress, bed , Lat. stragulum, vestis stragula, (Theognis Elegiacus):—;in plural the bedclothes, the coverings of a dinner-couch , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
2. a horsecloth, horse-trappings , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9213.definition:
a bed spread or prepared; generally, a bed, couch , (Pindar), etc.: a mattress, bedding , (Xenophon Historicus); στρ. ἄφθιτος, of the golden fleece, (Pindar) 
from στρώτης (ML)

G9214.definition:
1. hated, abhorred, hateful , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;with dative hateful or hostile to one, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. gloomy, sullen , Lat. tristis, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὁρᾶν στυγνός gloomy to behold, (Xenophon Historicus);—; στυγνὸς εἴκων yielding sullenly, with an ill grace , (Sophocles Tragicus); neuter as adverb, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9217.definition: made of the wood of the tree στύραξ, (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G9219.definition:
1. a writing or noting down , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. that which is written, a writing, book: a history, narrative , (Thucydides), etc. 
3. a written contract, a covenant, bond , Lat. syngrapha, (Thucydides); συγγ. ναυτικαί a bond to secure money lent on bottomry, (Demosthenes Orator); ἀνδριάντα ἐκδεδωκὼς κατὰ συγγραφήν having contracted for its execution, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9221.definition: set on fire with or at once, burn up , Lat. comburere, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9224.definition: to mix in with, mingle, blend with , Χάριτας Μούσαις συγκαταμιγνύς (Euripides):—;Pass. to be absorbed in a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9225.definition: to eat up, devour with or together , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9227.definition: to dwell with one, τινί (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9228.definition:
1. Pass. to lie together , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. as Pass. of συντίθημι, to be composed or compounded , ἔκ τινων of certain parts, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
3. of written works, to be composed , (Thucydides), etc. 
4. to be contrived, concocted , (Euripides), etc. 
5. to be agreed on by two parties, (Thucydides): in participle agreed on, arranged , αἱ συγκείμεναι ἡμέραι (Herdotus Historicus); κατὰ τὰ συγκείμενα according to the terms agreed on , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐκ τῶν ξυγκειμένων (Thucydides) 
6. impersonal σύγκειται, it has been or is agreed on , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; so, συγκειμένου σφι, with infinitive, since they had agreed to . . , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9231.definition: to break off :—;Pass. to be cramped , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9235.definition:
1. called together, summoned , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. ς. ἐκκλησία at Athens, an assembly specially summoned by the στρατηγός (opposite to the ordinary meetings, αἱ κυρίαι); Decret. quoted in (Demosthenes Orator):—;generally, σύγκλητος (i.e. ἐκκλησία); a legislative body , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G9238.definition:
1. to break up, cut up , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. to thrash soundly, pound well , (Xenophon Historicus);—;Pass., perfect infinitive συγκεκόφθαι (Aristophanes Comicus); participle συγκεκομμένος (Euripides) (ML)

G9239.definition: a mixing together, commixture, blending, tempering , (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

G9241.definition:
1. a compounding , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2. a comparing, comparison , (Aristotle Philosopher), etc. (ML)
